before.title: Doppler shift and aberration for an ideal plane wave between inertial descriptions
before.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model, and the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b with beta in R^3, |beta| < 1, b in R^4 and B(beta) the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost; write gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) and beta_hat := beta/|beta| for beta nonzero, so that the frame x' moves with velocity v = c beta relative to the frame x in the direction beta_hat. Let the ideal wave of the model have phase theta with future null wave covector k and frame-x data (omega,s) in the sense of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency: omega > 0, s in R^3 with |s| = 1 and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s) in x. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Frame data in x'. The data of the same covector k in x' is (omega',s') with omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and omega' = omega, s' = s for beta = 0), so |s'| = 1 and k'_a = (-omega'/c, (omega'/c)s'_1, (omega'/c)s'_2, (omega'/c)s'_3) in x'. In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and (s'_2,s'_3) = (s_2,s_3)/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (ii) Reading and frequency ratios. The rest observers of x and x' (four-velocities c e_0 and c e'_0) read angular frequencies omega = -c k(e_0) and omega' = -c k(e'_0); the linear frequencies and wavelengths of the two descriptions satisfy nu' = gamma(1 - beta . s) nu and lambda' = lambda/[gamma(1 - beta . s)]. More generally, an ideal observer whose coordinate velocity in x is w (a vector of the frame's spatial three-space with |w| < c) reads omega_o = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega, where gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^(-1/2); equivalently omega_o = gamma_w(1 - beta_w . s) omega with beta_w := w/c. (iii) Longitudinal cases. If s = beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) < omega, nu' = nu sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)): the observer moving in the direction of propagation (away from a source at rest in x and located behind it) reads a red-shifted frequency and lengthened wavelength. If s = -beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)) > omega and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)): blue shift for an observer moving opposite to the propagation direction (toward such a source). (iv) Transverse protocols. If beta . s = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x) then omega' = gamma omega > omega. If beta . s = |beta|^2, equivalently s' . beta_hat = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x'), then omega' = omega/gamma < omega. Both configurations are called transverse Doppler configurations in the literature and the two factors differ; the direction and size of the shift are not determined by the word 'transverse' without specifying the frame in which transversality holds. (v) Aberration. If theta_x, theta_x' in [0,pi] are the angles between the propagation directions s, s' and the boost axis beta_hat, then cos theta_x' = (cos theta_x - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta_x); the map u |-> (u - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| u) is a strictly increasing bijection of [-1,1] onto itself, and in particular cos theta_x = 0 gives cos theta_x' = -|beta|. (vi) Scope and protocol. All clauses concern one ideal plane wave and ideal observers, and frequencies are compared through the phase model at specified reception events; the results are conditional on the adopted postulates (ideal plane wave, ideal clocks, inertial covariance, flat classical spacetime) and are not empirical claims about nature, sources or apparatus. They exclude media and dispersion, modulation and signal speeds, intensity and polarization, real line widths, accelerating observers (reserved to the framework's accelerated-observer page), gravitation and quantum effects; no statistical or measurement statement is made. If beta = 0 the two charts agree and omega' = omega, s' = s.
before.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the mathematical core is lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation with the reading lemmas. (i) By def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency the frame data of k in x is (omega,s) with omega = c varpi, varpi = -k(e_0), and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s). Apply lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation(i)-(ii) with (varpi,s): its conclusions give varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and the displayed s' with |s'| = 1; multiplying by c gives omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega; the axis formulas are clause (iii) of the lemma. The relation beta . s = |beta|^2 <=> s' . beta_hat = 0 is clause (iv) of the lemma, and the identity s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(|beta|(1 - beta . s)) for beta nonzero is its display. (ii) For the rest observer of x, U = c e_0 and omega = -c k(e_0) by the definition; for x' likewise with the frame vector e'_0 (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). The wavelength ratio is the reciprocal of the frequency ratio because lambda = c/nu and lambda' = c/nu' by definition. For a general observer write U_o = gamma_w(c,w) by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(e); then k(U_o) = c gamma_w k(e_0) + gamma_w k(w), and k(w) = (omega/c) w . s because w lies in the frame's spatial three-space and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s) (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame); hence omega_o = -k(U_o) = gamma_w(omega - (omega/c) w . s) = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega. (iii) Substitute s = +/- beta_hat into (i): gamma(1 -/+ |beta|) = sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) because gamma^2(1 -/+ |beta|)^2 = (1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|); the wavelength ratios are the reciprocals. The receding/approaching identification uses the fixed protocol: the source is at rest in x and the wave propagates from it, so s = beta_hat means the x'-rest observer moves away from the source and s = -beta_hat means it moves toward it. (iv) beta . s = 0 gives omega' = gamma omega from (i); beta . s = |beta|^2 gives omega' = gamma(1 - |beta|^2) omega = omega/gamma, and the equivalence with s' . beta_hat = 0 is the displayed identity; the two cases are distinct because a unit s with beta . s = 0 is not a unit s with beta . s = |beta|^2 when |beta| > 0. The existence of both configurations for every |beta| < 1 is exhibited by the examples on the companion page. (v) Divide the axis formula s'_1 = (s_1 - beta)/(1 - beta s_1) by beta = |beta| for the component along beta_hat (equivalently use s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(|beta|(1 - beta . s)) and divide numerator and denominator by |beta|) to get cos theta_x' = (cos theta_x - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta_x); the map is the restriction of the Mobius map with positive derivative (1 - |beta|^2)/(1 - |beta| u)^2 > 0 on [-1,1] and fixes the endpoints +1, -1. (vi) The scope clause records the hypotheses and the exclusions; no step uses a source or detector model, and no choice principle is used. The postulate post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model supplies the physical interpretation of theta, k and the reading rule, and the two other postulates supply the model's light and covariance clauses; the deduction is conditional on all of them.

before.title: The proper orthochronous Lorentz group: boosts, rotations, unique factorization and invariants
before.statement: Let (V,eta) be the Lorentz vector space with time orientation C^+ and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model. Then: (i) For every beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 the passive boost B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, B(beta)^{-1} = B(-beta), and for collinear boosts B(beta_1 e)B(beta_2 e) = B(((beta_1 + beta_2)/(1 + beta_1 beta_2)) e) for every unit spatial vector e and beta_1, beta_2 in (-1,1); in particular collinear boosts commute. If beta is the parameter of B(beta), then beta = tanh r for a unique rapidity r in R, and collinear rapidities add. (ii) SO^+(V,eta) is a subgroup of O(V,eta), which is a subgroup of GL(V); every passive boost B(beta) and every spatial rotation of the frame (extended by fixing e_0) belongs to SO^+(V,eta). (iii) Every L in SO^+(V,eta) has a unique factorization L = B(-beta) Rhat with |beta| < 1 and Rhat the extension of a spatial rotation of the frame; here beta = u_vec/u^0 where (u^0,u_vec) are the coordinates of u = L e_0. Consequently every proper orthochronous Lorentz map is the product of a passive boost and a spatial rotation (in that order), and L is itself a passive boost if and only if the rotation is the identity. (iv) Every L in SO^+(V,eta) preserves the interval eta(v,v), the causal classification of every nonzero vector, the future and past closed cones, the orientation and the oriented volume form of the model: epsilon(Lv_0,...,Lv_3) = epsilon(v_0,...,v_3) for all v_0,...,v_3 in V. An arbitrary element L of O(V,eta) has det L = +-1 and either preserves or interchanges the future and past cones, and det L = 1 alone does not force L(C^+) = C^+.
before.strategy: Assembly of the page's proved lemmas, with each clause assigned to its supplier. (i) is lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse plus lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition plus the bijection r |-> tanh r of lem-rapidity-parametrization-of-collinear-boosts. (ii) is lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(ii) for the subgroup statements; boosts lie in SO^+(V,eta) by (i), and a spatial rotation Rhat is a Lorentz map fixing the future timelike vector e_0, hence proper of determinant one and orthochronous by lem-boost-rotation-factorization(iii). (iii) is lem-boost-rotation-factorization(ii),(iv),(v). (iv) combines lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) with det-preservation; the final sentence records the failure of the converse of 'proper implies orthochronous' and is witnessed by the B-page counterexample cex-sr-discrete-lorentz-maps-are-not-proper-orthochronous, whose claim is the explicit matrix computation, not an input here. The proof contract must restate the hypotheses (frame fixed, |beta| < 1, L proper orthochronous) and cite each lemma as the whole content of its clause; no clause may be asserted without the corresponding cited result.

before.title: Covariance, boosts and the two field invariants
before.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event $p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$, $F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then: (a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart, $$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$ equivalently, componentwise, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-vB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+vB_2)$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+vE_3/c^2)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-vE_2/c^2)$. (b) [Invariants] at every such $p$, $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$ equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in $x'$. (c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if $\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper orthochronous change of inertial chart acts on $(E,B)$ as the composition of the rotation law and the boost law of (a) in that order. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation from the transformation law, then the scalar contractions. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (b) The two expressions are the two independent scalar contractions of the two-form; substituting the component law into $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ with $\eta'=\eta$ shows invariance, equivalently clauses (c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) identifies them with $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$. (c) For the rotation case $\Lambda^0{}_0=1$, $\Lambda^0{}_j=\Lambda^i{}_0=0$, $\Lambda^i{}_j=R^i{}_j$ give $F'^{0i}=R^i{}_jF^{0j}$ and $F'^{ij}=R^i{}_kR^j{}_lF^{kl}$; reading the dictionary and using $\det R=1$ in the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{nij}R^i{}_kR^j{}_lR^n{}_m=\epsilon_{klm}$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]) gives $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along $\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$, including $v=0$, $$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$ At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is assigned. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (a′) For $v\ne0$ put $u=v/|v|$. Choose a coordinate vector $e_j$ not parallel to $u$, set $a=(e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u)/|e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u|$ and $b=u\times a$. Direct cross-product coordinates show $(u,a,b)$ is an oriented orthonormal basis. Let $R$ have these vectors as rows, so $Ru=e_1$, $R^{\mathsf T}R=I$ and $\det R=1$; only one finite choice is used. Substituting the matrix of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{-1}\Lambda_{|v|/c}\widehat R$. Apply the rotation component law proved in (c), then the axis computation (a), then rotate back. The determinant-one cofactor identity gives $R(p\times q)=(Rp)\times(Rq)$, yielding the parallel/perpendicular formulas. Use $\gamma_v-1=\gamma_v^2|v|^2/(c^2(\gamma_v+1))$ to combine the pieces into the displayed nonsingular vector formulas; at zero the separately defined boost is the identity. The general case is the actual unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii). Since components transform by multiplication with $\Lambda$, first apply $\widehat R$ and then $B(-\beta)$; the latter uses (a′) with vector velocity $-c\beta$, not the nonnegative axis parameter of (a). (d) Chain clauses (a)-(c) with [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: clause (a) of that theorem in both charts plus its clause (b) for the pair of descriptions. No potential, no second derivative of the fields, no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

before.title: Observer field split and exact classical wave Doppler reading
before.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e,b\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=b_0=0.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the musical isomorphisms taken with the positive rest metric of $n^\perp$; under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] for the parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), the longitudinal red-/blue-shift formulas, the two transverse configurations and the composition clause of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) applying verbatim to the readings of this wave. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** evaluate the observer decomposition of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] at the given $n$, then apply the exact SR Doppler theorem to the wave data. (a) $e_0=F_{0b}n^b=F_{0i}n^i=\gamma_wE_iw_i/c^2$? Compute directly: $e_a=F_{ab}n^b$ with $n^0=\gamma_w$, $n^i=\gamma_ww^i/c$: $e_0=F_{0i}n^i=(-E_i/c)(\gamma_ww_i/c)=-\gamma_wE\cdot w/c^2$, which vanishes because $e$ is a rest-space covector only after lowering with the rest metric — the clean computation is $e(n)=F(n,n)=0$ by antisymmetry, and $e_i=F_{i0}n^0+F_{ij}n^j=(E_i/c)\gamma_w+\epsilon_{ijk}B_k\gamma_ww_j/c=\gamma_w(E_i+(w\times B)_i)/c$ with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; likewise $b(n)=0$ and, using $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$, $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$ (the dual dictionary, clauses (a)-(b) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] applied to $*F$ with $*(*F)=-F$), $b_i=-\gamma_w(B_i-(w\times E)_i/c^2)$. The reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ is clause (a) of that theorem. The rest-frame components of $E_n=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n=-b^\sharp$ are the boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a) with $v=w$, since the rest frame of $n$ is related to the laboratory frame by the passive boost with parameter $w/c$ ([[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] for the linear map and [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e) for the identification of $w$). (b) The amplitude equations give $|k|=\omega/c$ and $s=k/|k|$ with $|s|=1$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (b)); raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=\omega/c>0$, $k^i=(\omega/c)s^i$ and $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$, so $k$ is future null and nonzero. The data $(\omega,s)$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]], whose clauses (i)-(v) give $\omega_n=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$, the aberrated direction and the longitudinal/transverse cases; the reading rule is clause (ii) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. (c) records the adopted interpretation premise (A1) and the scope; no choice principle is used and no empirical premise enters.
before.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth framework fields at one event: the decomposition of the field into the rest components of a future unit observer, the reconstruction of $F$, the measured electric and magnetic vectors of an inertial observer with coordinate velocity $w$, and the exact angular-frequency reading and aberration of an ideal plane wave, with the ideal-detector and ideal-plane-wave model assumptions stated. Excluded: apparatus calibration, real detectors, accelerated observers, media and dispersion, modulation, finite line widths, intensity and polarization measurement, quantum photon models, and any statistical or empirical claim.

after.title: Observer field split and exact classical wave Doppler reading
after.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e^\sharp,b^\sharp\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=-\frac{\gamma_w}{c^2}E\cdot w,\qquad b_0=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}B\cdot w.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the covectors first restricted to $n^\perp$ and raised with its positive rest metric (equivalently their spacetime metric-dual vectors, since both annihilate $n$); under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the arbitrary-direction boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′) for the vector parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. At $w=0$ the observer is the laboratory rest observer and reads $E,B$ themselves; there is no distinguished direction of motion. Orthogonality means $e(n)=b(n)=0$, not vanishing temporal covector components in an unrelated laboratory frame. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), longitudinal formulas and two transverse protocols of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) apply with their nonzero-motion qualifications; at $w=0$ frequency and direction are unchanged. Successive inertial changes act on the same phase covector by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii); each stage updates the direction as well as the frequency, and positive successive frequency ratios multiply. This composition statement is a direct covector/reading calculation, not a nonexistent composition clause of the Doppler supplier. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.
after.strategy: **Proof technique:** evaluate the observer decomposition of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] at the given $n$, then apply the exact SR Doppler theorem to the wave data. (a) Directly evaluate the adopted dictionary at $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$: $e_0=-\gamma_w E\cdot w/c^2$, $e_i=\gamma_w(E_i+(w\times B)_i)/c$. The dual dictionary is $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$, $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$, so $b_0=\gamma_w B\cdot w/c$ and $b_i=-\gamma_w(B_i-(w\times E)_i/c^2)$. In particular $n^ae_a=n^ab_a=0$, using $w\cdot(w\times B)=w\cdot(w\times E)=0$; antisymmetry gives the same annihilation intrinsically. Raising with the spacetime metric maps these annihilating covectors into $n^\perp$, and its restriction agrees with the positive rest-space musical isomorphism. The reconstruction is exactly [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a). The vector boost [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $w/c$ sends $n$ to $(1,0,0,0)$: its temporal component is $\gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2)=1$ and the spatial block cancels. Thus its primed oriented axes are the observer's canonical inertial rest axes. Apply the repaired arbitrary-direction law [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′); in those axes $e'_0=b'_0=0$, $E'_i=c e'_i$ and $B'_i=-b'_i$, giving exactly the measured-vector components under assumption (A1). For $w=0$ the boost is the identity. No rest-space metric lowering can erase a nonzero laboratory component; the two component descriptions are distinct. (b) The amplitude equations give $|k|=\omega/c$ and $s=k/|k|$ with $|s|=1$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (b)); raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=\omega/c>0$, $k^i=(\omega/c)s^i$ and $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$, so $k$ is future null and nonzero. The data $(\omega,s)$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]], whose clauses (i)-(v) give $\omega_n=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$, the aberrated direction and the longitudinal/transverse cases; the reading rule is clause (ii) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. For successive changes $x_1=\Lambda_1x_0+b_1$, $x_2=\Lambda_2x_1+b_2$, the covector laws give $k_2=(\Lambda_2^{-1})^{\mathsf T}(\Lambda_1^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0=((\Lambda_2\Lambda_1)^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0$. The affine phase constant transforms with the translations as in [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii). Apply the positive frequency reading at each stage, obtaining $\omega_2/\omega_0=(\omega_2/\omega_1)(\omega_1/\omega_0)$ with the correctly updated intermediate direction. (c) records the adopted interpretation premise (A1) and the scope; no choice principle is used and no empirical premise enters.
after.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth framework fields at one event: the decomposition of the field into the rest components of a future unit observer, the reconstruction of $F$, the measured electric and magnetic vectors of an inertial observer with coordinate velocity $w$, and the exact angular-frequency reading and aberration of an ideal plane wave, with the ideal-detector and ideal-plane-wave model assumptions stated. Excluded: apparatus calibration, real detectors, accelerated observers, media and dispersion, modulation, finite line widths, intensity and polarization measurement, quantum photon models, and any statistical or empirical claim.

before.title: The four-force equation reproduces the coordinate Lorentz force and power
before.statement: Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value theorem to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$. (a) With $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]) and $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U_\nu=\gamma(-c,v)$: $q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(F^i{}_0+F^i{}_jv^j/c\bigr)=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ since $F^i{}_0=\eta_{00}F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; and $q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. Since $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\Phi(U)^i$ and $d/dt=\gamma^{-1}d/d\tau$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)), $dp_i/dt=\gamma^{-1}\,q\gamma(E+v\times B)_i=q(E+v\times B)_i$ with $p=m\gamma v$ from [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a); the temporal component gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$ after multiplying by $c$. (b) $\eta(U,U)$ has derivative $2\eta(U,U')=2(q/m)\eta(U,\Phi(U))=0$ by the orthogonality clause of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] (which needs no derivative of the field); the initial value $-c^2$ is that of the four-velocity. (c) $z:=|v|^2/c^2$ and $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$; by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ with $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. First-order bound by the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $|f(z)-1|=|f'(\xi)|z\le z\,/\,(2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2})$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, using monotonicity of the positive power ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]). Second-order remainder by Cauchy's mean value theorem ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]) applied on $[0,z]$ to $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac s2$ and $g(s):=s^2$: $q(z)/z^2=q'(\xi)/g'(\xi)=(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12)/(2\xi)$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, and the mean value theorem on $[0,\xi]$ applied to $f'$ gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in(0,\xi)$, so $|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2|=\tfrac12|f''(\eta)|z^2\le\tfrac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
before.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one charged massive particle of constant charge and positive external rest mass moving on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed exterior electromagnetic field that is $C^1$ near the graph, under the adopted covariant coupling: the coordinate Lorentz force and power, preservation of the four-velocity norm, and uniform low-speed bounds with constants depending only on the speed interval. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction, self-force, magnetic monopoles, variable or zero mass, trajectory approximation over time without a stability argument, and any measurement or empirical claim.

before.title: The covariant field stress-energy tensor and its balance law
before.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: $E,B$ jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] with the additional derivatives required by each Maxwell equation existing and continuous, continuous sources $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components, $j=(cho,J)$ the four-current, $u$ and $S$ the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Define the stress-energy tensor of the field by $$T^{\mu
u}:= rac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(F^{\mu\alpha}F^
u{}_\alpha- rac14\eta^{\mu
u}F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}\Bigr).$$ Then: (a) [Object] $T$ is a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] with $\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}$ continuous on $U$, it is traceless, $\eta_{\mu
u}T^{\mu
u}=0$, and under a proper orthochronous change of inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$ its components transform as $T'^{\mu
u}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^
u{}_ eta T^{\alpha eta}$ ([[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). (b) [Components] in the laboratory frame $$T^{00}=u= rac{\varepsilon_0|E|^2}{2}+ rac{|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{0i}=T^{i0}= rac{S_i}{c}=c\,g_i= rac{(E	imes B)_i}{\mu_0c},\qquad T^{ij}=-\sigma_{ij},$$ where $\sigma_{ij}=\varepsilon_0 igl(E_iE_j-	frac12\delta_{ij}|E|^2 igr)+\mu_0^{-1} igl(B_iB_j-	frac12\delta_{ij}|B|^2 igr)$; in particular the spatial block is minus the Maxwell stress of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. (c) [Balance] under the smooth branch, $$\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}=-f^
u,\qquad f^
u:=F^{
u\lambda}j_\lambda,$$ where $f^
u$ is the Lorentz four-force density of the coupling, with the component identities $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ and $\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-(ho E+J	imes B)$ of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a). (d) [Matter coupling and finite-flux conservation] let $T_{\mathrm m}$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field on $U$ satisfying $\partial_\mu T_{\mathrm m}{}^{\mu
u}=f^
u$ (an adopted matter model, not derived here); then $\partial_\mu(T+T_{\mathrm m})^{\mu
u}=0$, the finite box and slice identities of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] hold for the total tensor with $f=0$, and the angular current $M^{\lambda\mu
u}:=x^\mu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda
u}-x^
u T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}$ satisfies $\partial_\lambda M^{\lambda\mu
u}=0$ by symmetry. before.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct algebra from the components for (a)-(b); the product rule and the cyclic identity for (c); summation and the finite-box theorem for (d). (a) Symmetry: $\eta_{\alpha eta}F^{\mu\alpha}F^{
u eta}=\eta_{\alpha eta}F^{\mu eta}F^{
u\alpha}$ by relabelling, and $\eta^{\mu
u}$ is symmetric; trace: $\eta_{\mu
u}T^{\mu
u}=\mu_0^{-1}(F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}-	frac14\cdot4\cdot F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta})=0$; the transformation law is contraction of two copies of the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii) with $\eta$ invariant, and the regularity is the component criterion of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] (every term is a polynomial in the $C^1$ components). u}=(\partial_\mu F^{\mu\alpha})F^
u{}_\alpha+F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^
u{}_\alpha-	frac12F^{\alpha eta}\partial^
u F_{\alpha eta}$; the first factor is $-\mu_0j^\alpha$ by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] ((TM1)), giving $-f^
u$; contracting the cyclic identity (TM2) of that theorem with $F^{\mu\alpha}$ kills the bracket exactly as in the research computation ($F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F_{ eta\alpha}=	frac14\partial_ eta(F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta})$, the two other terms coinciding by antisymmetry and relabelling). before.title: Boosted uniform electric field and the mixed magnetic field
before.statement: Let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and consider the constant fields of [[def-em-fields]] $$E:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3,\quad E\equiv E_0e_2,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ which form a source-free smooth solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (all first derivatives vanish and $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$). Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the boosted inertial chart of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]]. Then the components of the same field in $x'$ are $$E'=\gamma E_0\,e_2,\qquad B'=-\frac{\gamma\beta E_0}{c}\,e_3=-\frac{\gamma vE_0}{c^2}\,e_3,$$ so the moving observer reads an electric field of magnitude $\gamma E_0$ along $e_2$ and, for $\beta>0$, a nonzero magnetic field along $-e_3$: a purely electric uniform field acquires a magnetic component in the boosted description. The two invariants check directly: with the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2\Bigl(\frac{\beta^2E_0^2}{c^2}-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}\Bigr)=-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B,$$ using $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]). At $\beta=0$ the formulas reduce to $E'=E$, $B'=0$. The computation is exact for the constant field; the example reports no measurement, identifies no source producing the field, and asserts nothing about finite-energy or bounded configurations.
before.strategy: **Verification:** substitute the data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] with $\beta$ as given. Here $E_\parallel=0$, $B_\parallel=0$ since $E\perp e_1$ and $B=0$, and $v\times B=0$, while $v\times E=v e_1\times E_0e_2=vE_0e_3$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the boost formulas give $E'=\gamma E_0e_2$ and $B'=-\gamma vE_0e_3/c^2=-\gamma\beta E_0e_3/c$. The invariant values are computed with [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the identity $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]; the constant field is a solution of the source-free smooth branch because every displayed first derivative vanishes. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
before.physical_scope: An exact algebraic example for one uniform static electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_2$, $B\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) and one passive boost along $e_1$ with $0\le\beta<1$: the boosted components, the resulting mixed magnetic field and the two field invariants. Excluded: real sources of the uniform field, boundary or finite-support configurations, measurements and any empirical claim.

before.title: Exact trajectory in a uniform electric field and the failure of the unscoped Newtonian extrapolation
before.statement:
Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter, $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass and $E_0>0$ a field strength in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and consider the prescribed exterior field of [[def-em-fields]] $$E\equiv E_0e_1,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ a source-free constant solution of the smooth vacuum Maxwell branch. Put $h:=qE_0/(mc)$, carrying the unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$, and for $r_0\in\mathbb R^3$ define the chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ by $$r(t):=r_0+ rac{c}{h} igl(\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}-1 igr)e_1\quad(h
e0),\qquad r(t):=r_0\quad(h=0),$$ $$v(t):=r'(t)= rac{c\,ht}{\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}}\,e_1\ (h
e0),\qquad \gamma(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2},\qquad p(t):=m\gamma(t)v(t).$$ Then: (i) [Exact solution] for $h
e0$ the curve is a future timelike $C^\infty$ curve with coordinate velocity $v(t)$, $|v(t)|<c$ for every finite $t$ and $|v(t)|	o c$ as $t	o\pm\infty$, and $p(t)=qE_0t\,e_1$, so that $$ rac{dp}{dt}=qE_0e_1=q(E+v	imes B),\qquad  rac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$$ hold identically, as required by [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (a); at $h=0$ (equivalently $q=0$) the curve is the constant $r\equiv r_0$ with $v\equiv0$, $p\equiv0$ and the same equations hold trivially. (ii) [Energy] $\gamma(t)mc^2=mc^2\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ and $ rac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$: the field delivers power $qE\cdot v$ to the particle. (iii) [Unscoped Newtonian extrapolation] the Newtonian constant-acceleration prediction $v_N(t):=(qE_0/m)t\,e_1$ satisfies $v(t)=v_N(t)/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$, so the two agree only to first order in $|ht|$ and $|v_N(t)|=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}\,|v(t)|$ exceeds $c$ for $|t|>1/|h|$, whereas the exact solution of the adopted coupling remains subluminal at every finite time; the Newtonian trajectory is a low-speed approximation in the sense of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c) and is not an exact consequence of the adopted coupling. (iv) [Scope] the field is prescribed and external, the particle's own field and any radiation reaction or self-force are excluded, and no measurement or empirical claim is made; the solution is exact for the stated coupling with $E_0>0$ and arbitrary constant $q$.
before.strategy: **Verification:** direct differentiation and substitution. For $h\ne0$ set $g(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$; by [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the map $t\mapsto(1+h^2t^2)^{1/2}$ is differentiable with $g'(t)=h^2t/g(t)$ ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]), hence $r'(t)=(c/h)g'(t)e_1=chte_1/g(t)=v(t)$ and $|v(t)|/c=|ht|/g(t)<1$ because $h^2t^2<1+h^2t^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]), with $|v(t)|\to c$ as $|t|\to\infty$. Then $p(t)=m\gamma(t)v(t)=mc\,ht\,e_1=qE_0t\,e_1$, so $dp/dt=qE_0e_1$, and $q(E+v\times B)=qE_0e_1$ since $B=0$ and $v\times0=0$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the power identity is $\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=mc^2h^2t/g(t)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$. The curve is future timelike: its tangent $(c,v(t))$ has $\eta$-square $-c^2+|v(t)|^2<0$ with positive time component, in the sense of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a) and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the vector-valued derivative is [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. Part (iii) is the displayed identity $v=v_N/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ with $v_N=(qE_0/m)te_1=hct\,e_1$, whose norm exceeds $c$ exactly when $|ht|>1$. The $h=0$ case is the constant curve. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
before.physical_scope: An exact conditional solution example for one prescribed uniform external electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_1$, $B\equiv0$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) acting on a particle of constant charge $q$ and external rest mass $m>0$ under the framework's adopted covariant coupling: the trajectory, its subluminality at all finite times, the work-energy identity, and the comparison with the unscoped Newtonian constant-acceleration extrapolation. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and self-force, the production of the field, measurement, and any empirical claim.

Put $r_N(t)=r_0+	frac12hc t^2e_1$. For $h
e0$, $$|v-v_N|\le rac c2|ht|^3,\qquad |r-r_N|\le rac{c}{8|h|}|ht|^4.$$ Thus on $|ht|\le\delta$ the velocity error is at most $c\delta^3/2$ and the displacement error at most $c\delta^4/(8|h|)$; these are special-model comparisons, not a general trajectory-stability consequence of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c). before.title: Tensor Maxwell equations equal the four laboratory Maxwell equations
before.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ with its inertial chart $x$, the electric and magnetic fields $E,B$ of [[def-em-fields]], the source fields $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]] with $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be those of the framework, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with the components fixed there, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let $j=(cho,J)$ carry the tensor-component identification adopted in [[def-em-sources]]. Assume the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]: $E,B$ are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega	imes I$ with the additional derivatives required by each displayed equation existing and continuous, and $ho,J$ are continuous. Write $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ and $\partial_i$ for the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and $\operatorname{div},\operatorname{curl}$ for those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then: (a) [Equivalence] On $I	imes\Omega$ the four smooth-branch equations $$\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ hold if and only if the two systems $$(\mathrm{TM1})\quad \partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0\,j^
u\ (
u=0,1,2,3),\qquad (\mathrm{TM2})\quad \partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}=0\ (\lambda,\mu,
u\in\{0,1,2,3\})$$ hold on $I	imes\Omega$. Every instance of $(\mathrm{TM2})$ with a repeated index vanishes identically because $F$ is alternating, so $(\mathrm{TM1})$ and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ carry exactly eight independent scalar equations: $(\mathrm{TM1})$ with $
u=0$ is $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ (using $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$), $(\mathrm{TM1})$ with $
u=i$ is the $i$-th component of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, $(\mathrm{TM2})$ with $(\lambda,\mu,
u)=(1,2,3)$ is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and the three cyclic triples $(0,i,j)$ are the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$; conversely these eight scalar equations reproduce the two systems. (b) [Form invariance under a change of inertial description] Let $x'$ be another inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$, $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix (the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]), and let the primed components of the same objects be the tensor components of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii): $F'^{\,ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$, $F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$, $j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$. Then $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x$ if and only if $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x'$ with $j'$, and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in $x'$; by (a) applied in both charts the four smooth-branch equations are likewise form-invariant, the primed fields satisfying the primed equations with the primed sources. (c) [Hypotheses actually used] Only first derivatives of $E,B$ occur; the equivalence uses exactly the component dictionary, the alternating character of $F$, the constants $\mu_0,c,\varepsilon_0$ and the identification $j=(cho,J)$, and the covariance clause uses the constant-coefficient component law and the invertibility of $\Lambda$. No potential, no second derivative, no boundary, decay or smoothness hypothesis beyond the stated class, and no converse from the wave equations to the Maxwell equations is used or asserted. (d) [Scope] Only the smooth branch is covered; the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and field or source points of singular support are excluded. The conventions $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ fix the signs of $(\mathrm{TM1})$, and the alternative sign convention, which reverses the form of the sourced equation, is not mixed with them. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates, uses no choice principle and makes no empirical claim.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation, then the transformation law. (a) Substitute the displayed components: $\partial_\mu F^{\mu0}=\partial_iF^{i0}=-\operatorname{div}E/c$ versus $-\mu_0j^0=-\mu_0c\rho$ gives $\operatorname{div}E=\mu_0c^2\rho=\rho/\varepsilon_0$; $\partial_\mu F^{\mu i}=\partial_0F^{0i}+\partial_jF^{ji}=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i-(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$ versus $-\mu_0j^i$ gives the $i$-th Ampère component; $\partial_1F_{23}+\partial_2F_{31}+\partial_3F_{12}=\operatorname{div}B$; and the cyclic sums $\partial_0F_{ij}+\partial_iF_{j0}+\partial_jF_{0i}=c^{-1}\left(\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_tB_k+\partial_iE_j-\partial_jE_i\right)$ for the three cyclic pairs $(i,j)$ give the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. Each display is an identity after substituting the components, so both implications follow; no derivative is commuted and no epsilon-identity beyond the coordinate definition of the components is used. (b) For $(\mathrm{TM1})$: $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\Lambda^a{}_e\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{ef}=\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{cf}$ by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iv) and orthogonality $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$, so $\partial_cF^{cf}=-\mu_0j^f$ is equivalent to $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=-\mu_0j'^b$. For $(\mathrm{TM2})$ the three derivative factors contribute the same trilinear factor $(\Lambda^{-1})^{\otimes3}$ to the cyclic sum, and $\Lambda^{-1}$ is invertible; hence zero is preserved in both directions. No physical equivalence of descriptions is proved: clause (b) is conditional on the adoption of [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]].
before.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell postulate on the laboratory region: the four SI Maxwell equations are equivalent to the two tensor equations for the components of the electromagnetic two-form and four-current fixed by [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and [[def-em-sources]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $x^0=ct$, $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$, and form-invariance under proper orthochronous changes of inertial chart. Excluded: the weak branch, singular source support, magnetic charge, potentials, and any dynamics beyond the adopted equations; no empirical claim.

(b) For $(\mathrm{TM1})$: $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\Lambda^a{}_e\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{ef}=\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{cf}$ by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iv) and orthogonality $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$, so $\partial_cF^{cf}=-\mu_0j^f$ is equivalent to $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=-\mu_0j'^b$. For $(\mathrm{TM2})$ the three derivative factors contribute the same trilinear factor $(\Lambda^{-1})^{\otimes3}$ to the cyclic sum, and $\Lambda^{-1}$ is invertible; hence zero is preserved in both directions. No physical equivalence of descriptions is proved: clause (b) is conditional on the adoption of [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]].

before.title: Covariance, boosts and the two field invariants
before.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event $p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$, $F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then: (a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart, $$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$ equivalently, componentwise, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-vB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+vB_2)$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+vE_3/c^2)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-vE_2/c^2)$. (b) [Invariants] at every such $p$, $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$ equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in $x'$. (c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if $\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper orthochronous change of inertial chart acts on $(E,B)$ as the composition of the rotation law and the boost law of (a) in that order. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation from the transformation law, then the scalar contractions. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (b) The two expressions are the two independent scalar contractions of the two-form; substituting the component law into $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ with $\eta'=\eta$ shows invariance, equivalently clauses (c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) identifies them with $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$. (c) For the rotation case $\Lambda^0{}_0=1$, $\Lambda^0{}_j=\Lambda^i{}_0=0$, $\Lambda^i{}_j=R^i{}_j$ give $F'^{0i}=R^i{}_jF^{0j}$ and $F'^{ij}=R^i{}_kR^j{}_lF^{kl}$; reading the dictionary and using $\det R=1$ in the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{nij}R^i{}_kR^j{}_lR^n{}_m=\epsilon_{klm}$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]) gives $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$. The general case is the unique factorization of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii), applied in the stated order. (d) Chain clauses (a)-(c) with [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: clause (a) of that theorem in both charts plus its clause (b) for the pair of descriptions. No potential, no second derivative of the fields, no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

Excluded: accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, media, weak or singular fields, orientation-reversing changes, apparatus and any measurement or empirical claim.

after.title: Covariance, boosts and the two field invariants
after.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event $p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$, $F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then: (a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart, $$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$ equivalently, componentwise, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$. (a′) [Arbitrary boost direction] For a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v|<c$, use the actual vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]], with $\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along $\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$, including $v=0$, $$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$ At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is assigned.  (b) [Invariants] at every such $p$, $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$ equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in $x'$. (c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if $\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper orthochronous change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the arbitrary-direction boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\beta$, where $\beta$ is the vector parameter of that factorization. The axis-only law (a) is not substituted for a general vector boost. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).
after.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation from the transformation law, then the scalar contractions. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (a′) For $v\ne0$ put $u=v/|v|$. Choose a coordinate vector $e_j$ not parallel to $u$, set $a=(e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u)/|e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u|$ and $b=u\times a$. Direct cross-product coordinates show $(u,a,b)$ is an oriented orthonormal basis. Let $R$ have these vectors as rows, so $Ru=e_1$, $R^{\mathsf T}R=I$ and $\det R=1$; only one finite choice is used. Substituting the matrix of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{-1}\Lambda_{|v|/c}\widehat R$. Apply the rotation component law proved in (c), then the axis computation (a), then rotate back. The determinant-one cofactor identity gives $R(p\times q)=(Rp)\times(Rq)$, yielding the parallel/perpendicular formulas. Use $\gamma_v-1=\gamma_v^2|v|^2/(c^2(\gamma_v+1))$ to combine the pieces into the displayed nonsingular vector formulas; at zero the separately defined boost is the identity.  (b) The two expressions are the two independent scalar contractions of the two-form; substituting the component law into $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ with $\eta'=\eta$ shows invariance, equivalently clauses (c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) identifies them with $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$. (c) For the rotation case $\Lambda^0{}_0=1$, $\Lambda^0{}_j=\Lambda^i{}_0=0$, $\Lambda^i{}_j=R^i{}_j$ give $F'^{0i}=R^i{}_jF^{0j}$ and $F'^{ij}=R^i{}_kR^j{}_lF^{kl}$; reading the dictionary and using $\det R=1$ in the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{nij}R^i{}_kR^j{}_lR^n{}_m=\epsilon_{klm}$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]) gives $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$. The general case is the actual unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii). Since components transform by multiplication with $\Lambda$, first apply $\widehat R$ and then $B(-\beta)$; the latter uses (a′) with vector velocity $-c\beta$, not the nonnegative axis parameter of (a). (d) Chain clauses (a)-(c) with [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: clause (a) of that theorem in both charts plus its clause (b) for the pair of descriptions. No potential, no second derivative of the fields, no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

before.title: Observer field split and exact classical wave Doppler reading
before.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e,b\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=b_0=0.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the musical isomorphisms taken with the positive rest metric of $n^\perp$; under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] for the parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), the longitudinal red-/blue-shift formulas, the two transverse configurations and the composition clause of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) applying verbatim to the readings of this wave. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** evaluate the observer decomposition of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] at the given $n$, then apply the exact SR Doppler theorem to the wave data. (a) $e_0=F_{0b}n^b=F_{0i}n^i=\gamma_wE_iw_i/c^2$? Compute directly: $e_a=F_{ab}n^b$ with $n^0=\gamma_w$, $n^i=\gamma_ww^i/c$: $e_0=F_{0i}n^i=(-E_i/c)(\gamma_ww_i/c)=-\gamma_wE\cdot w/c^2$, which vanishes because $e$ is a rest-space covector only after lowering with the rest metric — the clean computation is $e(n)=F(n,n)=0$ by antisymmetry, and $e_i=F_{i0}n^0+F_{ij}n^j=(E_i/c)\gamma_w+\epsilon_{ijk}B_k\gamma_ww_j/c=\gamma_w(E_i+(w\times B)_i)/c$ with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; likewise $b(n)=0$ and, using $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$, $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$ (the dual dictionary, clauses (a)-(b) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] applied to $*F$ with $*(*F)=-F$), $b_i=-\gamma_w(B_i-(w\times E)_i/c^2)$. The reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ is clause (a) of that theorem. The rest-frame components of $E_n=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n=-b^\sharp$ are the boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a) with $v=w$, since the rest frame of $n$ is related to the laboratory frame by the passive boost with parameter $w/c$ ([[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] for the linear map and [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e) for the identification of $w$). (b) The amplitude equations give $|k|=\omega/c$ and $s=k/|k|$ with $|s|=1$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (b)); raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=\omega/c>0$, $k^i=(\omega/c)s^i$ and $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$, so $k$ is future null and nonzero. The data $(\omega,s)$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]], whose clauses (i)-(v) give $\omega_n=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$, the aberrated direction and the longitudinal/transverse cases; the reading rule is clause (ii) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]].
