after.title: Observer field split and exact classical wave Doppler reading
after.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e^\sharp,b^\sharp\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=-\frac{\gamma_w}{c^2}E\cdot w,\qquad b_0=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}B\cdot w.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the covectors first restricted to $n^\perp$ and raised with its positive rest metric (equivalently their spacetime metric-dual vectors, since both annihilate $n$); under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the arbitrary-direction boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′) for the vector parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. At $w=0$ the observer is the laboratory rest observer and reads $E,B$ themselves; there is no distinguished direction of motion. Orthogonality means $e(n)=b(n)=0$, not vanishing temporal covector components in an unrelated laboratory frame. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), longitudinal formulas and two transverse protocols of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) apply with their nonzero-motion qualifications; at $w=0$ frequency and direction are unchanged. Successive inertial changes act on the same phase covector by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii); each stage updates the direction as well as the frequency, and positive successive frequency ratios multiply. This composition statement is a direct covector/reading calculation, not a nonexistent composition clause of the Doppler supplier. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.
after.strategy: **Proof technique:** evaluate the observer decomposition of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] at the given $n$, then apply the exact SR Doppler theorem to the wave data. (a) Directly evaluate the adopted dictionary at $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$: $e_0=-\gamma_w E\cdot w/c^2$, $e_i=\gamma_w(E_i+(w\times B)_i)/c$. The dual dictionary is $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$, $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$, so $b_0=\gamma_w B\cdot w/c$ and $b_i=-\gamma_w(B_i-(w\times E)_i/c^2)$. In particular $n^ae_a=n^ab_a=0$, using $w\cdot(w\times B)=w\cdot(w\times E)=0$; antisymmetry gives the same annihilation intrinsically. Raising with the spacetime metric maps these annihilating covectors into $n^\perp$, and its restriction agrees with the positive rest-space musical isomorphism. The reconstruction is exactly [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a). The vector boost [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $w/c$ sends $n$ to $(1,0,0,0)$: its temporal component is $\gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2)=1$ and the spatial block cancels. Thus its primed oriented axes are the observer's canonical inertial rest axes. Apply the repaired arbitrary-direction law [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′); in those axes $e'_0=b'_0=0$, $E'_i=c e'_i$ and $B'_i=-b'_i$, giving exactly the measured-vector components under assumption (A1). For $w=0$ the boost is the identity. No rest-space metric lowering can erase a nonzero laboratory component; the two component descriptions are distinct. (b) The amplitude equations give $|k|=\omega/c$ and $s=k/|k|$ with $|s|=1$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (b)); raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=\omega/c>0$, $k^i=(\omega/c)s^i$ and $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$, so $k$ is future null and nonzero. The data $(\omega,s)$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]], whose clauses (i)-(v) give $\omega_n=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$, the aberrated direction and the longitudinal/transverse cases; the reading rule is clause (ii) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. For successive changes $x_1=\Lambda_1x_0+b_1$, $x_2=\Lambda_2x_1+b_2$, the covector laws give $k_2=(\Lambda_2^{-1})^{\mathsf T}(\Lambda_1^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0=((\Lambda_2\Lambda_1)^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0$. The affine phase constant transforms with the translations as in [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii). Apply the positive frequency reading at each stage, obtaining $\omega_2/\omega_0=(\omega_2/\omega_1)(\omega_1/\omega_0)$ with the correctly updated intermediate direction. (c) records the adopted interpretation premise (A1) and the scope; no choice principle is used and no empirical premise enters.

before.title: The four-force equation reproduces the coordinate Lorentz force and power
before.statement: Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value theorem to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$. (a) With $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]) and $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U_\nu=\gamma(-c,v)$: $q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(F^i{}_0+F^i{}_jv^j/c\bigr)=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ since $F^i{}_0=\eta_{00}F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; and $q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. Since $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\Phi(U)^i$ and $d/dt=\gamma^{-1}d/d\tau$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)), $dp_i/dt=\gamma^{-1}\,q\gamma(E+v\times B)_i=q(E+v\times B)_i$ with $p=m\gamma v$ from [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a); the temporal component gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$ after multiplying by $c$. (b) $\eta(U,U)$ has derivative $2\eta(U,U')=2(q/m)\eta(U,\Phi(U))=0$ by the orthogonality clause of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] (which needs no derivative of the field); the initial value $-c^2$ is that of the four-velocity. (c) $z:=|v|^2/c^2$ and $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$; by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ with $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. First-order bound by the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $|f(z)-1|=|f'(\xi)|z\le z\,/\,(2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2})$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, using monotonicity of the positive power ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]). Second-order remainder by Cauchy's mean value theorem ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]) applied on $[0,z]$ to $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac s2$ and $g(s):=s^2$: $q(z)/z^2=q'(\xi)/g'(\xi)=(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12)/(2\xi)$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, and the mean value theorem on $[0,\xi]$ applied to $f'$ gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in(0,\xi)$, so $|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2|=\tfrac12|f''(\eta)|z^2\le\tfrac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
before.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one charged massive particle of constant charge and positive external rest mass moving on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed exterior electromagnetic field that is $C^1$ near the graph, under the adopted covariant coupling: the coordinate Lorentz force and power, preservation of the four-velocity norm, and uniform low-speed bounds with constants depending only on the speed interval. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction, self-force, magnetic monopoles, variable or zero mass, trajectory approximation over time without a stability argument, and any measurement or empirical claim.

At $z=0$ all stated differences and bounds are zero directly; henceforth assume $0<z\le\delta^2$. First-order bound by the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $|f(z)-1|=|f'(\xi)|z\le z\,/\,(2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2})$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, using monotonicity of the positive power ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]). Second-order remainder by Cauchy's mean value theorem ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]) applied on $[0,z]$ to $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac s2$ and $g(s):=s^2$: $q(z)/z^2=q'(\xi)/g'(\xi)=(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12)/(2\xi)$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, and the mean value theorem on $[0,\xi]$ applied to $f'$ gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in(0,\xi)$, so $|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2|=\tfrac12|f''(\eta)|z^2\le\tfrac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
after.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one charged massive particle of constant charge and positive external rest mass moving on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed exterior electromagnetic field that is $C^1$ near the graph, under the adopted covariant coupling: the coordinate Lorentz force and power, preservation of the four-velocity norm, and uniform low-speed bounds with constants depending only on the speed interval. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction, self-force, magnetic monopoles, variable or zero mass, trajectory approximation over time without a stability argument, and any measurement or empirical claim.

before.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: $E,B$ jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] with the additional derivatives required by each Maxwell equation existing and continuous, continuous sources $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components, $j=(cho,J)$ the four-current, $u$ and $S$ the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. before.title: Boosted uniform electric field and the mixed magnetic field
before.statement: Let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and consider the constant fields of [[def-em-fields]] $$E:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3,\quad E\equiv E_0e_2,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ which form a source-free smooth solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (all first derivatives vanish and $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$). Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the boosted inertial chart of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]]. Then the components of the same field in $x'$ are $$E'=\gamma E_0\,e_2,\qquad B'=-\frac{\gamma\beta E_0}{c}\,e_3=-\frac{\gamma vE_0}{c^2}\,e_3,$$ so the moving observer reads an electric field of magnitude $\gamma E_0$ along $e_2$ and, for $\beta>0$, a nonzero magnetic field along $-e_3$: a purely electric uniform field acquires a magnetic component in the boosted description. The two invariants check directly: with the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2\Bigl(\frac{\beta^2E_0^2}{c^2}-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}\Bigr)=-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B,$$ using $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]). At $\beta=0$ the formulas reduce to $E'=E$, $B'=0$. The computation is exact for the constant field; the example reports no measurement, identifies no source producing the field, and asserts nothing about finite-energy or bounded configurations.
before.strategy: **Verification:** substitute the data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] with $\beta$ as given. Here $E_\parallel=0$, $B_\parallel=0$ since $E\perp e_1$ and $B=0$, and $v\times B=0$, while $v\times E=v e_1\times E_0e_2=vE_0e_3$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the boost formulas give $E'=\gamma E_0e_2$ and $B'=-\gamma vE_0e_3/c^2=-\gamma\beta E_0e_3/c$. The invariant values are computed with [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the identity $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]; the constant field is a solution of the source-free smooth branch because every displayed first derivative vanishes. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
before.physical_scope: An exact algebraic example for one uniform static electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_2$, $B\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) and one passive boost along $e_1$ with $0\le\beta<1$: the boosted components, the resulting mixed magnetic field and the two field invariants. Excluded: real sources of the uniform field, boundary or finite-support configurations, measurements and any empirical claim.

before.title: Exact trajectory in a uniform electric field and the failure of the unscoped Newtonian extrapolation
before.statement:
Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter, $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass and $E_0>0$ a field strength in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and consider the prescribed exterior field of [[def-em-fields]] $$E\equiv E_0e_1,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ a source-free constant solution of the smooth vacuum Maxwell branch. Put $h:=qE_0/(mc)$, carrying the unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$, and for $r_0\in\mathbb R^3$ define the chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ by $$r(t):=r_0+ rac{c}{h} igl(\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}-1 igr)e_1\quad(h
e0),\qquad r(t):=r_0\quad(h=0),$$ $$v(t):=r'(t)= rac{c\,ht}{\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}}\,e_1\ (h
e0),\qquad \gamma(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2},\qquad p(t):=m\gamma(t)v(t).$$ Then: (i) [Exact solution] for $h
e0$ the curve is a future timelike $C^\infty$ curve with coordinate velocity $v(t)$, $|v(t)|<c$ for every finite $t$ and $|v(t)|	o c$ as $t	o\pm\infty$, and $p(t)=qE_0t\,e_1$, so that $$ rac{dp}{dt}=qE_0e_1=q(E+v	imes B),\qquad  rac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$$ hold identically, as required by [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (a); at $h=0$ (equivalently $q=0$) the curve is the constant $r\equiv r_0$ with $v\equiv0$, $p\equiv0$ and the same equations hold trivially. (ii) [Energy] $\gamma(t)mc^2=mc^2\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ and $ rac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$: the field delivers power $qE\cdot v$ to the particle. (iii) [Unscoped Newtonian extrapolation] the Newtonian constant-acceleration prediction $v_N(t):=(qE_0/m)t\,e_1$ satisfies $v(t)=v_N(t)/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$, so the two agree only to first order in $|ht|$ and $|v_N(t)|=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}\,|v(t)|$ exceeds $c$ for $|t|>1/|h|$, whereas the exact solution of the adopted coupling remains subluminal at every finite time; the Newtonian trajectory is a low-speed approximation in the sense of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c) and is not an exact consequence of the adopted coupling. (iv) [Scope] the field is prescribed and external, the particle's own field and any radiation reaction or self-force are excluded, and no measurement or empirical claim is made; the solution is exact for the stated coupling with $E_0>0$ and arbitrary constant $q$.
before.strategy: **Verification:** direct differentiation and substitution. For $h\ne0$ set $g(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$; by [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the map $t\mapsto(1+h^2t^2)^{1/2}$ is differentiable with $g'(t)=h^2t/g(t)$ ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]), hence $r'(t)=(c/h)g'(t)e_1=chte_1/g(t)=v(t)$ and $|v(t)|/c=|ht|/g(t)<1$ because $h^2t^2<1+h^2t^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]), with $|v(t)|\to c$ as $|t|\to\infty$. Then $p(t)=m\gamma(t)v(t)=mc\,ht\,e_1=qE_0t\,e_1$, so $dp/dt=qE_0e_1$, and $q(E+v\times B)=qE_0e_1$ since $B=0$ and $v\times0=0$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the power identity is $\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=mc^2h^2t/g(t)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$. The curve is future timelike: its tangent $(c,v(t))$ has $\eta$-square $-c^2+|v(t)|^2<0$ with positive time component, in the sense of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a) and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the vector-valued derivative is [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. Part (iii) is the displayed identity $v=v_N/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ with $v_N=(qE_0/m)te_1=hct\,e_1$, whose norm exceeds $c$ exactly when $|ht|>1$. The $h=0$ case is the constant curve. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
before.physical_scope: An exact conditional solution example for one prescribed uniform external electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_1$, $B\equiv0$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) acting on a particle of constant charge $q$ and external rest mass $m>0$ under the framework's adopted covariant coupling: the trajectory, its subluminality at all finite times, the work-energy identity, and the comparison with the unscoped Newtonian constant-acceleration extrapolation. consumer_reviews.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model, and the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b with beta in R^3, |beta| < 1, b in R^4 and B(beta) the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost; write gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) and beta_hat := beta/|beta| for beta nonzero, so that the frame x' moves with velocity v = c beta relative to the frame x in the direction beta_hat. Let the ideal wave of the model have phase theta with future null wave covector k and frame-x data (omega,s) in the sense of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency: omega > 0, s in R^3 with |s| = 1 and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s) in x. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Frame data in x'. The data of the same covector k in x' is (omega',s') with omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and omega' = omega, s' = s for beta = 0), so |s'| = 1 and k'_a = (-omega'/c, (omega'/c)s'_1, (omega'/c)s'_2, (omega'/c)s'_3) in x'. In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and (s'_2,s'_3) = (s_2,s_3)/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (ii) Reading and frequency ratios. The rest observers of x and x' (four-velocities c e_0 and c e'_0) read angular frequencies omega = -c k(e_0) and omega' = -c k(e'_0); the linear frequencies and wavelengths of the two descriptions satisfy nu' = gamma(1 - beta . s) nu and lambda' = lambda/[gamma(1 - beta . s)]. More generally, an ideal observer whose coordinate velocity in x is w (a vector of the frame's spatial three-space with |w| < c) reads omega_o = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega, where gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^(-1/2); equivalently omega_o = gamma_w(1 - beta_w . s) omega with beta_w := w/c. (iii) Longitudinal cases. If s = beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) < omega, nu' = nu sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)): the observer moving in the direction of propagation (away from a source at rest in x and located behind it) reads a red-shifted frequency and lengthened wavelength. If s = -beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)) > omega and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)): blue shift for an observer moving opposite to the propagation direction (toward such a source). (iv) Transverse protocols. If beta . s = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x) then omega' = gamma omega; this is greater than omega when beta!=0 and equals omega when beta=0. If beta . s = |beta|^2, for beta!=0 equivalently s' . beta_hat = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x'), then omega' = omega/gamma; this is less than omega when beta!=0 and equals omega when beta=0. Both configurations are called transverse Doppler configurations in the literature and the two factors differ for beta!=0 (both equal one at beta=0); the direction and size of the shift are not determined by the word 'transverse' without specifying the frame in which transversality holds. (v) Aberration. For beta!=0, if theta_x, theta_x' in [0,pi] are the angles between the propagation directions s, s' and the boost axis beta_hat, then cos theta_x' = (cos theta_x - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta_x); the map u |-> (u - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| u) is a strictly increasing bijection of [-1,1] onto itself, and in particular cos theta_x = 0 gives cos theta_x' = -|beta|. (vi) Scope and protocol. All clauses concern one ideal plane wave and ideal observers, and frequencies are compared through the phase model at specified reception events; the results are conditional on the adopted postulates (ideal plane wave, ideal clocks, inertial covariance, flat classical spacetime) and are not empirical claims about nature, sources or apparatus. They exclude media and dispersion, modulation and signal speeds, intensity and polarization, real line widths, accelerating observers (reserved to the framework's accelerated-observer page), gravitation and quantum effects; no statistical or measurement statement is made. If beta = 0 the transition is the pure translation x'=x+b: the inertial axes and wave-covector frame data agree, with omega'=omega and s'=s, while the affine phase constant is transformed as in the covector/phase law.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the mathematical core is lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation with the reading lemmas. (i) By def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency the frame data of k in x is (omega,s) with omega = c varpi, varpi = -k(e_0), and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s). Apply lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation(i)-(ii) with (varpi,s): its conclusions give varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and the displayed s' with |s'| = 1; multiplying by c gives omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega; the axis formulas are clause (iii) of the lemma. The relation beta . s = |beta|^2 <=> s' . beta_hat = 0 is clause (iv) of the lemma, and the identity s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(|beta|(1 - beta . s)) for beta nonzero is its display. (ii) For the rest observer of x, U = c e_0 and omega = -c k(e_0) by the definition; for x' likewise with the frame vector e'_0 (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). The wavelength ratio is the reciprocal of the frequency ratio because lambda = c/nu and lambda' = c/nu' by definition. For a general observer write U_o = gamma_w(c,w) by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(e); then k(U_o) = c gamma_w k(e_0) + gamma_w k(w), and k(w) = (omega/c) w . s because w lies in the frame's spatial three-space and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s) (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame); hence omega_o = -k(U_o) = gamma_w(omega - (omega/c) w . s) = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega. (iii) Substitute s = +/- beta_hat into (i): gamma(1 -/+ |beta|) = sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) because gamma^2(1 -/+ |beta|)^2 = (1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|); the wavelength ratios are the reciprocals. The receding/approaching identification uses the fixed protocol: the source is at rest in x and the wave propagates from it, so s = beta_hat means the x'-rest observer moves away from the source and s = -beta_hat means it moves toward it. (iv) beta . s = 0 gives omega' = gamma omega from (i); beta . s = |beta|^2 gives omega' = gamma(1 - |beta|^2) omega = omega/gamma, and the equivalence with s' . beta_hat = 0 is the displayed identity; at beta=0 both read omega'=omega and no direction beta_hat is assigned; for nonzero beta, gamma>1 gives the stated strict inequalities. The two protocols are distinct because a unit s with beta . s = 0 is not a unit s with beta . s = |beta|^2 when |beta| > 0. The existence of both configurations for every |beta| < 1 is exhibited by the examples on the companion page. (v) For beta!=0 set b:=|beta| and use the invariant display s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - b^2)/(b(1 - beta . s)). Substitute beta . s=b cos theta_x and cancel the strictly positive b to obtain cos theta_x'=(cos theta_x-b)/(1-b cos theta_x). No division of a coordinate axis formula by beta is used. The denominator is positive on [-1,1] because 0<b<1, and the derivative of u |-> (u-b)/(1-bu) is (1-b^2)/(1-bu)^2>0; its endpoint values are -1 and1, so it is the stated strictly increasing bijection. At beta=0 frequency/direction data agree and no boost-axis angle is assigned. (vi) The scope clause records the hypotheses and the exclusions; no step uses a source or detector model, and no choice principle is used. The postulate post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model supplies the physical interpretation of theta, k and the reading rule, and the two other postulates supply the model's light and covariance clauses; the deduction is conditional on all of them.

consumer_reviews.statement:
**Statement refuted.** A declared one-point data record of the vocabulary with positive declared uncertainty determines the parameter of an operational model uniquely: if a record R of clause (c) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] is consistent with two parameters $\beta_1,\beta_2$ of one operational model M, then $\beta_1=\beta_2$.

**Counterexample.** Adopt the SI convention $x^0=ct$ and the ideal plane-wave/frequency-reading model of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]], conditionally as in [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]. Fix an inertial chart x and a positive angular frequency $\omega$. For every $\beta\in(-1,1)$ let $x'=B(\beta e_1)x$ be the passive boosted inertial chart; use an ideal emitter at rest in x, the future null wave covector with frame-x components $(-\omega/c,\omega/c,0,0)$ and propagation direction $s=e_1$, and the straight rest observer of x'. Let $S=\Theta=(-1,1)$, $\theta=\mathrm{id}$ and let $D(\beta)$ be this finite declared run description. The Doppler theorem gives $\omega_o=\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)\omega$, where $\gamma_\beta=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, so the dimensionless prediction is $$F(\beta)=\frac{\omega_o}{\omega}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\beta}{1+\beta}}.$$ Thus $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ satisfies the operational vocabulary's interpretation condition (*), with $d=1$; the interpretation is a conditional model computation, not an apparatus claim. Use the explicitly declared comparison rule that a parameter is consistent with a one-point scalar record exactly when its prediction lies in that record's declared closed interval.

Take the illustrative record $N=1$, $z_1=z=9/10$, $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon=1/100$ and annotation 'longitudinal Doppler ratio of the moving observer in the propagation direction'. consumer_reviews.statement: Remark on the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions and def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency, for use with pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration. (a) Units in the adopted coordinates x^0 = c t: the phase theta is dimensionless; the coordinates x^a, the wavelength lambda and all distances are in metres; the components k_a of a wave covector, the wave vector kappa and varpi = -k(e_0) are in m^-1; the angular frequencies omega and omega_n and the linear frequencies nu are in s^-1 (nu also in hertz); c is in m s^-1; and s, beta, beta_w and gamma are dimensionless. (b) Two coordinate forms. In the adopted coordinates theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s); in a chart whose time coordinate is t in seconds directly, so that the metric component g_tt = -c^2 carries m^2 s^-2 and the time-space components carry m s^-1, the same phase is theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const with the same omega and kappa, and the component tuple (-omega, (omega/c)s) carries mixed units; formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other. This is the general warning of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions specialized to the wave covector. (c) Natural units and restoration. In natural units c = 1 with x^0 = t one has k_a = (-omega, omega s), lambda = 2 pi/omega, and the Doppler and aberration factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) are unchanged; restoring dimensions means replacing k_0 by -omega/c, k_i by (omega/c)s_i, writing every velocity as v = c beta with the dimensionless beta, and replacing lambda by 2 pi c/omega = c/nu. The dimensionless factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and the longitudinal square roots need no c restoration because they contain only beta, s and gamma; the c restoration affects the map between omega, nu, lambda and the components of k, not the shift factors themselves. (d) This remark introduces no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content and no measurement claim; it is a units and convention statement carrying the scope of the items it cites.

consumer_reviews.statement: Let (V,eta) be the Lorentz vector space with time orientation C^+ and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model. Then: (i) For every beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 the passive boost B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, B(beta)^{-1} = B(-beta), and for collinear boosts B(beta_1 e)B(beta_2 e) = B(((beta_1 + beta_2)/(1 + beta_1 beta_2)) e) for every unit spatial vector e and beta_1, beta_2 in (-1,1); in particular collinear boosts commute. For each fixed unit spatial axis e and scalar b in (-1,1), the collinear boost B(b e) has b = tanh r for a unique scalar rapidity r in R; rapidities add for boosts along that same fixed axis. This signed scalar rapidity statement does not identify a vector beta in R^3 with the scalar tanh r. (ii) SO^+(V,eta) is a subgroup of O(V,eta), which is a subgroup of GL(V); every passive boost B(beta) and every spatial rotation of the frame (extended by fixing e_0) belongs to SO^+(V,eta). (iii) Every L in SO^+(V,eta) has a unique factorization L = B(-beta) Rhat with |beta| < 1 and Rhat the extension of a spatial rotation of the frame; here beta = u_vec/u^0 where (u^0,u_vec) are the coordinates of u = L e_0. Consequently every proper orthochronous Lorentz map is the product of a passive boost and a spatial rotation (in that order), and L is itself a passive boost if and only if the rotation is the identity. (iv) Every L in SO^+(V,eta) preserves the interval eta(v,v), the causal classification of every nonzero vector, the future and past closed cones, the orientation and the oriented volume form of the model: epsilon(Lv_0,...,Lv_3) = epsilon(v_0,...,v_3) for all v_0,...,v_3 in V. An arbitrary element L of O(V,eta) has det L = +-1 and either preserves or interchanges the future and past cones, and det L = 1 alone does not force L(C^+) = C^+.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Assembly of the page's proved lemmas, with each clause assigned to its supplier. The vector boost claims use vector beta; only B(b e) with a specified unit axis uses signed scalar b and r. (ii) is lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(ii) for the subgroup statements; boosts lie in SO^+(V,eta) by (i), and a spatial rotation Rhat is a Lorentz map fixing the future timelike vector e_0, hence proper of determinant one and orthochronous by lem-boost-rotation-factorization(iii). (iii) is lem-boost-rotation-factorization(ii),(iv),(v). (iv) combines lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) with det-preservation; the final sentence records the failure of the converse of 'proper implies orthochronous' and is witnessed by the B-page counterexample cex-sr-discrete-lorentz-maps-are-not-proper-orthochronous, whose claim is the explicit matrix computation, not an input here. The proof contract must restate the hypotheses (frame fixed, |beta| < 1, L proper orthochronous) and cite each lemma as the whole content of its clause; no clause may be asserted without the corresponding cited result.

consumer_reviews.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Let $|\beta|<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that its primed coordinate velocity is $-\beta c\,e_1\prime$, with speed $|\beta|c$), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the adapted-frame numerical contraction is $T^{ab}(e_0\prime)_a(e_0\prime)_b=T\prime{}^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$. Its difference from $\varepsilon$ is $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$, so equality holds if and only if $\beta=0$ or $\varepsilon+P=0$. It is at least $\varepsilon$ whenever $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; no positivity of $\varepsilon+P$ is assumed here. The transverse diagonal components remain $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to identify this numerical contraction; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The adapted-frame numerical contraction is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used. Subtracting $\varepsilon$ gives $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$, and $\gamma^2-1=\beta^2/(1-\beta^2)$ vanishes exactly for $\beta=0$. Thus equality also holds for every boost when $\varepsilon+P=0$, and the inequality has exactly the stated conditional sign.

consumer_reviews.statement: Let $(V,\eta)$ be the oriented Lorentz vector space of the affine Minkowski model with orientation and volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], and let $F:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be an alternating bilinear form ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]). Define the Hodge dual by $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and set $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$. Use the standard form normalization $F=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}F_{ab}\theta^a\wedge\theta^b$ in the dual coframe $\theta^a(e_b)=\delta^a_b$ of an oriented orthonormal frame, and define $(F\wedge F)(v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3):=2[F(v_0,v_1)F(v_2,v_3)-F(v_0,v_2)F(v_1,v_3)+F(v_0,v_3)F(v_1,v_2)]$, the alternating four-form exterior square. Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and put $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$. (a) $e(n)=b(n)=0$, and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat:=\eta(n,\cdot)$; also $*(*F)=-F$, so the Hodge dual squares to $-1$ on two-forms. (b) In an oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}$, $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; hence the six components of $F$ are exactly the six components of the pair $(e,b)$ and the reconstruction in (a) is equivalent to these component formulae. (c) The quadratic invariants are $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,(e\cdot b)$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are those of the spatial structure of the frame ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); also $F\wedge F=2(e\cdot b)\varepsilon$. The two scalar expressions $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ form a basis of the homogeneous quadratic polynomials in the six components of $F$ invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group; the square-wedge expression is dependent, $F\wedge F=-\tfrac12 I_2\varepsilon$. $I_2$ is an oriented pseudoscalar and changes sign if the chosen orientation is reversed with the metric and $F$ held fixed. (d) (Optional SI identification.) Let $c>0$. If in an inertial frame one identifies $F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for spatial vector fields $E,B$, then $e_i=-E_i/c$ and $b_i=B_i$, the invariants of (c) read $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,(E\cdot B)/c$, and $F\wedge F=-2(E\cdot B)\varepsilon/c$. If $\kappa:=(F\wedge F)(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=(F\wedge F)_{0123}$, then $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. Under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta\in(-1,1)$ one has $E'_1=E_1$, $B'_1=B_1$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$ where the cross product is the right-handed product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v=\beta c$ along $e_1$. (e) The theorem is algebra on the oriented Lorentz vector space with the stated index and duality conventions; clause (d) is an explicitly optional identification of the components of $F$ with fields the electromagnetic framework names $E,B$, and the theorem asserts no field equation, no dynamics, no measurement and no transformation beyond the stated component law. No choice principle is used.
consumer_reviews.strategy: First obtain an oriented rest frame adapted to $n$: the observer decomposition theorem proves $n^\perp$ is a three-dimensional positive inner-product space ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)); apply finite Gram–Schmidt to a basis of it ([[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]) and reverse one spatial basis vector if the resulting frame orientation is negative. This uses only finite choices. Let $a_i=\theta^0\wedge\theta^i$ and $s_1=\theta^2\wedge\theta^3$, $s_2=\theta^3\wedge\theta^1$, $s_3=\theta^1\wedge\theta^2$. The declared dual and volume conventions give $*a_i=-s_i$, $*s_i=a_i$ by direct component evaluation. Thus $*^2=-1$ on all six basis forms, $F=-e_i a_i-b_i s_i$ and $*F=-b_i a_i+e_i s_i$, proving the annihilation, six-component recovery and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$. Raise the time-spatial indices with the diagonal metric and count both orders of each skew pair to get $\frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4e\cdot b$. The explicitly normalized square wedge has $a_i\wedge s_i=\varepsilon$ and all unmatched terms zero, so $F\wedge F=2e\cdot b\,\varepsilon$; the witness $F_{01}=F_{23}=1$ gives $e_1=b_1=-1$ and square wedge $+2\varepsilon$. The tensor/volume laws ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii),(v)) show that these expressions are invariant under proper Lorentz changes. For completeness of the quadratic invariant claim, spatial half-turns force the three coefficient blocks of a rotation-invariant quadratic polynomial to be diagonal, and proper axis permutations force scalar diagonals; it has the form $A|e|^2+B|b|^2+C e\cdot b$. For $e=(0,1,0),b=0$, an axis-one passive boost gives $e'=(0,\gamma,0),b'=(0,0,\gamma\beta)$; invariance gives $A(\gamma^2-1)+B\gamma^2\beta^2=0$, whence $A+B=0$ for any nonzero allowed $\beta$. Both surviving invariant polynomials are linearly independent by testing $b=0,e\ne0$ and $e=b\ne0$. For the optional SI identification, apply the actual passive boost matrix to the two raised indices of $F$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). All six entries are $E'_1=E_1$, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-vB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+vB_2)$, $B'_1=B_1$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+vE_3/c^2)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-vE_2/c^2)$, which are exactly the promised vector formulas with the right-handed cross product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Substituting $e=-E/c,b=B$ gives the displayed invariants and standard four-form coefficient $\kappa=-2E\cdot B/c$, hence $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. The zero-boost case gives $\gamma=1$ directly. All arguments are finite-dimensional, choice-free algebra and assert no EM dynamics. The cached Carroll full-text equations (1.79)–(1.88), printed pp.21–23, were read for wedge normalization and the Lorentzian star-square rule; the S8 local research route is independently recomputed, not accepted by citation.

This is the complete weak mixed-derivative cancellation using compact Riemann test identities, with no choice assumption and no narrowing to $C^2$ potentials. The spatial curl/gradient dictionary is the exact coordinate definition [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] at fixed time. Clause (d) restates the raised-index operator of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. No physical law is proved and no empirical claim is made.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
consumer_reviews.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

consumer_reviews.statement:
In the ideal grounded-plane configuration of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]]: vacuum half-space $H=\{x_3>0\}$, point charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ at $p=ae_3$ ($a>0$), field $E_I$ given by the image potential, and $E_I$ has the Coulomb singularity $(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))(x-p)/|x-p|^3$ of the source charge as $x\to p$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d), [[def-em-fields]]). Split the field near $p$ as
$$E_I(x)=E_q(x)+E_{\rm ext}(x),\qquad E_q(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{x-p}{|x-p|^3}\quad(x\ne p),$$
the **self-field** $E_q$ of the source charge and the **external (mirror) field** $E_{\rm ext}:=E_I-E_q$, which is $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $p$ (it is minus the gradient of the smooth mirror term $-q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)|x+ae_3|^{-1}$). Then:
(a) [External field at the charge] the external field at the location of the charge is
$$E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\frac{q}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}\,e_3 .$$
It is the gradient of the mirror term evaluated at $p$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).
(b) [Force on the held charge] under the adopted external Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i) at zero velocity, a test particle of charge $q$ held at $p$ experiences the electric force
$$F=q\,E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\frac{q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}\,e_3,$$
attractive toward the plane, of magnitude $q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$; the particle's own field is excluded from the coupling by the postulate, so the result is a two-body-style external force of the mirror field and is not a self-force.
(c) [Reading and scope] for either sign of $q$ the force is attractive (the magnitude depends on $q^2$); the induced total plane charge is $-q$ and its distribution is concentrated under the charge; the example is the exact ideal-model result for a held point charge, an ideal grounded plane and the adopted static external force law. It asserts no measurement, no dynamics of the charge (no motion or radiation), no finite-plane or finite-conductor correction, no self-force and no claim that the pair of idealisations is realised by an apparatus; the source is the idealised stationary point charge of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]](e), not a declared compact-source model.

consumer_reviews.statement: This example is conditional on the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the definitions of divergence and curl in [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], the equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]; all equalities below are equalities of units, using $1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$, $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{F}=1\ \mathrm{C\,V^{-1}}$ and $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$. (a) $\operatorname{div}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$ and $\rho/\varepsilon_0$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}/(F\,m^{-1})}=\mathrm{C\,V\,m^{-2}\,C^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$, so the two sides of $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ agree. (b) $\operatorname{curl}B$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $\mu_0J$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}\cdot A\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $c^{-2}\partial_tE$ has unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}\,s^{2}\cdot V\,m^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, so both source terms of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ have the unit of $\operatorname{curl}B$. (c) $\operatorname{curl}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$ and $\partial_tB$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ is homogeneous; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ is a homogeneous equation. (d) In the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], $qE$ has unit $\mathrm{C\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$ and $q\,(r'\times B)$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m\,s^{-1}\,T}=\mathrm{C\,N\,A^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$, so the two force terms add with the unit of a force; and $\rho E+J\times B$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}\,V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, the unit of a force density. (e) The energy density $\tfrac12(\varepsilon_0E^2+B^2/\mu_0)$ has unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and the flux $E\times B/\mu_0$ has unit $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, consistent with $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\cdot m\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. (f) The check is exact arithmetic of the adopted units; it is not a measurement, it does not prove the equations, and no numerical value of $\mu_0$ is used or asserted.

The only structural input is that divergence divides a field unit by a length and curl does the same while preserving the field unit ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); time derivatives divide by a time. All computations are finite and exact, and no empirical premise or measurement is used.

consumer_reviews.strategy: Write $E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)=E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support and integrate term by term. For (a), the constant term of the force gives $\bigl(\int\rho\,d\lambda_3\bigr)E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=QE_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$, and the constant term of the torque gives $\bigl(\int\rho(y)\,y\,d\lambda_3(y)\bigr)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ by linearity of the integral on $L^1$ and the bilinearity of the cross product ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). For the force remainder, if $R_F\ne0$ test it against the unit vector $u:=R_F/|R_F|$: $|R_F|=u\cdot R_F=\int\rho(y)\,u\cdot\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|\,|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le La\|\rho\|_1$, using $u\cdot v\le|v|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), the triangle and monotonicity rules for the integral ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support; the case $R_F=0$ is trivial. For the torque remainder, $\bigl|\int\rho(y)\,y\times\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\bigr|\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|y|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|^2|\rho|\,d\lambda_3\le La^2\|\rho\|_1$, using $|y\times v|\le|y|\,|v|$ ([[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Since the two integrals are absolutely convergent, all interchanges are finitely many applications of linearity and the triangle rule. For (b) insert $Q=0$. For (c), subtract and add $o$: $\int\rho(y)(y-o)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)d\lambda_3=\tau-o\times F$ by linearity and bilinearity of the cross product. For (d): at an instant of zero coordinate velocity the four-velocity has chart components $U=(c,0,0,0)$, hence $U_0=\eta_{0\mu}U^\mu=-c$ and $U_i=0$ ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b),(c)); the adopted equation [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (i) then gives $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q'F^{i0}U_0=q'(-E_i/c)(-c)=q'E^i$ because $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a)). Summing the two instantaneous forces and computing the moments about the origin by finite sums gives the displayed force and torque, with $p=q(d/2)+(-q)(-d/2)=qd$ by [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c) and the bound $|R_\tau|\le|q|\,(a)\,(2La)=2|q|La^2$; the same expansion as (a) applies with the total variation $2|q|$ ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]). Clause (e) records the model assumptions. Countable Choice is used only through the Lebesgue integrals and their suppliers; the Lipschitz constant and the field values enter only through the displayed estimates, and the norm continuity of [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]] is used to read the pointwise bounds. Changing $\rho$ on a $\lambda_3$-null set changes no integral ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

The potential exists by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]] with $E=-
abla\varphi$ and $\varphi\in C^2$; in particular $\varphi$ is $C^1$, and $\gamma$ is piecewise $C^1$ with values in the open set $\Omega$, so [[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]] applies on every $C^1$ piece: the line integral of $
abla\varphi$ equals the endpoint increment. Applying the vector line integral definitions of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]] to $qE=-q
abla\varphi$, the constant $q$ factors out of the integral and the increments of the pieces telescope at the interior partition points ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), leaving
$$W(\gamma)=-q\int_\gamma
abla\varphi\cdot d\mathbf r=q\, igl(\varphi(\gamma(t_0))-\varphi(\gamma(t_1)) igr),$$
which is (a). Claim (b) is immediate from (a) because the right-hand side depends only on the endpoints; a closed path has equal endpoints, so its work vanishes. Claim (c) is the definition $U=q\varphi$ and rearrangement, with $q$ in coulombs and $\varphi$ in volts ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Claim (d): two $C^2$ potentials of the same field differ by a constant on each piecewise-$C^1$ path component ([[cor-potentials-differ-by-a-componentwise-constant]]); a star-shaped $\Omega$ is path-connected through the segments to the centre, so the constant is global and the difference $\varphi(\gamma(t_0))-\varphi(\gamma(t_1))$ is unchanged ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). No dynamics is used: the path is prescribed, the force is the adopted external electric coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i), and in the pure electrostatic regime $B=0$ so no magnetic term appears in that coupling ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](b)).

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the Lebesgue, polar and surface interfaces cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\rho\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with support in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), let $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ be the smooth-branch Coulomb solution of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](a) with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], and let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ kernel, $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ ([[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). Then:
(a) [Finiteness] the three quantities
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3,\qquad +\frac{1}{2\varepsilon_0}\iint_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3}\Phi(x-y)\rho(x)\rho(y)\,d(\lambda_3\times\lambda_3)(x,y)$$
are finite real numbers;
(b) [Identity] they are equal:
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon_0}\iint_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3}\Phi(x-y)\rho(x)\rho(y)\,d(\lambda_3\times\lambda_3)(x,y).$$
The last expression is the **external assembly work** of the ideal quasistatic bookkeeping family $\rho_s=s\rho$, $\varphi_s=s\varphi$ for $0\le s\le1$. An added test charge brought from infinity, where the potential is zero, has electric-force work $-dq\,\varphi_s$ by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-work]]; the balancing external work is $+dq\,\varphi_s$. Therefore $W_{\rm ext}=\int_0^1s\,ds\int\rho\varphi=\tfrac12\int\rho\varphi$. Both signs of $\rho$ are allowed. The symmetric double kernel gives the equivalent ordered-pair interpretation of the factor $1/2$.
(c) [Scope] the identity is a statement about the ideal quasi-static assembly of a compactly supported $C^1$ charge distribution in vacuum, all sources being held in place by external support ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]). It asserts no time-dependent work, no radiation, no material or stability model, and it does not identify the field energy with the rest mass of any particle; the point-source limit is treated separately and is divergent (see the point-charge field energy of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d)).
consumer_reviews.strategy:
The compact continuous source is Borel and the kernel with finite pole assignment is Borel; the double-kernel integrands are therefore Borel/product measurable by [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], and their Euclidean and product-measure integrals agree by [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]]. Finiteness: $\varphi\in C^2$ and $E\in C^1$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](a)); on the bounded set $\overline B_{2R}$ the continuous $|E|^2$ is bounded ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]) and the ball has finite Lebesgue measure, while outside $\{|x|>2R\}$ one has $|E(x)|\le\|ho\|_1/(\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2)$ ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]], [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](a)), so $\int_{|x|>2R}|E|^2\le\|ho\|_1^2/(\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2)\int_{|x|>2R}|x|^{-4}d\lambda_3<\infty$ by the polar formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], with $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ from $|S^{n-1}|=n|B_1|$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], and $|B_1|=4\pi/3$, [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]) and $\int_{2R}^{\infty}r^{-2}dr<\infty$; the first integral is finite ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). The second integral is finite because $ho$ is bounded with compact support and $\varphi$ is continuous ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]). For the double integral, the integrand is measurable and $\iint|\Phi(x-y)||ho(x)||ho(y)|d\lambda_3d\lambda_3=\int|ho(x)| igl(\int\Phi(x-y)|ho(y)|dy igr)dx$; put $M=\|ho\|_\infty$. Uniformly in $x$, split the inner integral at $|x-y|=1$. On the near part the polar formula and translation invariance give $\int_{|x-y|<1}\Phi(x-y)|ho(y)|dy\le M(4\pi)^{-1}4\pi\int_0^1r\,dr=M/2$; on the far part it is at most $\|ho\|_1/(4\pi)$. Hence the absolute double integral is bounded by $\|ho\|_1(M/2+\|ho\|_1/(4\pi))<\infty$ via [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] and [[thm-integrals-are-invariant-under-measure-preserving-maps]], with translations preserving measure by [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]. No unproved continuity of $N|ho|$ is invoked.
(b) For $R'>R$ consider the ball $B_{R'}$, a bounded $C^1$ domain with outward normal $x/|x|$ on its boundary sphere $S_{R'}$ ([[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]]); Green's first identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with $u=v=\varphi$ gives
$$\int_{B_{R'}} igl(\varphi\Delta\varphi+|
abla\varphi|^2 igr)d\lambda_3=\int_{S_{R'}}\varphi\,\partial_
u\varphi\,dS.$$
Substituting $-\Delta\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](a)) and rearranging,
$$\int_{B_{R'}}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3= rac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{B_{R'}}ho\varphi\,d\lambda_3+\int_{S_{R'}}\varphi\,\partial_
u\varphi\,dS.$$
The boundary term tends to $0$: $|\int_{S_{R'}}\varphi\partial_

This gives the first equality of (b); the eventual constancy also identifies the limit with the integral over all of $\mathbb R^3$. For the second equality, insert $\varphi(x)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\int\Phi(x-y)ho(y)d\lambda_3(y)$ ([[def-newtonian-potential]], [[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]]): $\intho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\iintho(x)\Phi(x-y)ho(y)\,d\lambda_3(x)d\lambda_3(y)$ by Fubini ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]) applied to the integrable product (finiteness as in (a)); the kernel is symmetric, $\Phi(x-y)=\Phi(y-x)$, so the ordered-pair integral equals twice the unordered-pair sum, which is the displayed factor $	frac12$. consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $Q\in\mathbb R$, let $\overline B_a=\{x:|x|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and define, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]]),
$$\rho(x):=\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\,\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<a\}}(x),\qquad
E(x):=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\begin{cases}x/a^3,&|x|<a,\\ x/|x|^3,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad
\varphi(x):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{Q(3a^2-|x|^2)}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3},&|x|\le a,\\[6pt]\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|},&|x|\ge a.\end{cases}$$
(The value of $\rho$ on the sphere $\{|x|=a\}$ is immaterial: it is a Lebesgue-null set by the polar calculation $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$, since the one-dimensional singleton has measure zero ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]).) Then:
(a) [Regularity and gradient] $E$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$, of class $C^\infty$ on each of the open regions $\{|x|<a\}$, $\{|x|>a\}$; $\varphi\in C^1(\mathbb R^3)$, its displayed branch derivatives agree on $\{|x|=a\}$, and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]);
(b) [Classical equations] for every $x$ with $|x|\ne a$,
$$\operatorname{div}E(x)=\rho(x)/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E(x)=0$$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]);
(c) [Weak equations] the pair $(E,(\rho,0))$ satisfies the spatial distributional equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$: $E$ is $C^1$ on each side of the sphere $S_a=\{|x|=a\}$ with one-sided continuous traces that agree, $[E]=0$, so [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] gives
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=\{\operatorname{curl}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=0,$$
with $\rho$ the displayed locally integrable density and no surface-charge term ([[def-em-weak-sources]], [[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]] for the sphere as a compact embedded smooth hypersurface); by the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e) these are the weak equations of the static model for this source, with zero singular part;
(d) [Energy] the field energy is finite and equals the assembly integral,
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a},$$
computed with the polar formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]); the value agrees with the smooth-source identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] although the density here is only piecewise continuous;
(e) [Consistency and contrast] for $|x|>a$ the field is exactly the point-charge Coulomb field of total charge $Q$ centred at the origin ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) with $x_0=0$) although the source is the extended ball, and for $|x|<a$ it is the affine field $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$; $\varphi$ is continuous at $|x|=a$ and decays at infinity; the field is bounded on $\mathbb R^3$, so no divergence of field energy occurs for the extended source;
(f) [Scope] the example verifies the displayed candidate and its energy; it does not claim uniqueness of the solution (this would require boundary data and an infinity condition, and the density is not continuous), it asserts no empirical content, and the density $\rho$ is treated as a bounded $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ density with the sphere carrying no surface charge ($[E]=0$).
consumer_reviews.strategy:
For (a): on $\{|x|<a\}$, $E$ is the affine map $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$ and on $\{|x|>a\}$ it is $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$; both are $C^\infty$ on their open domains ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). At $|x|=a$ the two formulas coincide ($x/a^3=x/a^3$), so $E$ is continuous on all of $\mathbb R^3$ ([[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]]). For $\varphi$, the interior branch has gradient $-Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$ and the exterior branch has gradient $-Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$ by the chain rule, and the two gradients agree on $\{|x|=a\}$; the matching derivatives also exist on the interface, as follows. Let $F(r)$ be the displayed radial potential profile on $r\ge0$. Its two branches agree at $a$, and their one-sided derivatives both equal $-Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$, so the difference quotient $(F(a+h)-F(a))/h$ has that common limit from either sign. Thus $F$ is differentiable at $a$, and its derivative is continuous there by the branch formulas. Since $x\mapsto|x|$ is differentiable near each point of $S_a$, the chain rule proves actual total differentiability of $\varphi=F(|x|)$ there and gives the matching gradient. At the origin the interior polynomial already gives smoothness. The resulting partial derivatives exist and are continuous everywhere, whence $\varphi$ is $C^1$ with $\nabla\varphi=-E$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).
For (b): inside, $\operatorname{div}(Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3))=3Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and the curl of an affine field vanishes ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); outside, $\operatorname{div}(Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3))=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_i\partial_i(x_i|x|^{-3})=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}(3|x|^{-3}-3|x|^{-3})=0$ and the curl components $\partial_j(x_k|x|^{-3})-\partial_k(x_j|x|^{-3})=0$ vanish by the same direct differentiation ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), matching $\rho=0$ outside.
For (c): the set $S_a$ is a compact embedded smooth hypersurface with unit normal $n=x/|x|$, and the two sides $\Omega_-=\{|x|<a\}$, $\Omega_+=\{|x|>a\}$ are open; $E$ is $C^1$ on each side and its one-sided traces agree on $S_a$ (from (a)), so $[E]=F_+-F_-=0$ in the notation of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] applies: the distributional divergence is the piecewise classical divergence plus $n\cdot[E]\delta_{S_a}=0$, and the distributional curl is the piecewise classical curl plus $n\times[E]\delta_{S_a}=0$. By (b) the piecewise divergence is $\rho/\varepsilon_0$ as a locally integrable function and the piecewise curl is $0$; the sphere is null by applying [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] to its Borel indicator: $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$. A singleton is contained in intervals of arbitrarily small length, so its one-dimensional measure is zero; [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] then applies, and the pairing conventions are those of [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. The static reading is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e), and the source objects are those of [[def-em-weak-sources]] with zero singular part.
For (d): by the polar formula and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]) one has $\int_{B_a}|x|^2\,d\lambda_3=4\pi\int_0^ar^4\,dr=\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}$ and $\int_{B_a}d\lambda_3=\frac{4\pi a^3}{3}$; hence
$$\int_{B_a}|E|^2=\Bigl(\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3}\Bigr)^2\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}=\frac{Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0^2a},\qquad \int_{|x|>a}|E|^2=\frac{Q^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2}\cdot 4\pi\int_a^\infty r^{-2}dr=\frac{Q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2a},$$
using $\int_a^\infty r^{-2}dr=1/a$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]] and monotone convergence, [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); the sum times $\varepsilon_0/2$ is $\frac{Q^2}{40\pi\varepsilon_0a}+\frac{Q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a}=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a}$. The assembly integral is computed from the same two radial integrals, $\frac12\int\rho\varphi=\frac12\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\frac{Q}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3}\bigl(3a^2\frac{4\pi a^3}{3}-\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}\bigr)=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a}$, so the identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] extends to this piecewise-continuous bounded density by direct verification; the density is bounded with compact support and all integrands are continuous off a null sphere ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]).
For (e): the exterior branch equals the formula of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) with $q=Q$, $x_0=0$; $\varphi$ is continuous at $|x|=a$ since both branches give $Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a)$, and decays like $1/|x|$; $|E|\le |Q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, so the energy of (d) is finite and no point singularity arises. For (f): no uniqueness or empirical statement is used anywhere; the sphere's zero jump is exactly the checked equality of the two branches on $\{|x|=a\}$. The one-dimensional singleton used in the polar null-sphere calculation is null by [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]]. Finite-interval integrations of the continuous one-variable test/radial integrands above use [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] to identify their Riemann/FTC values with their Lebesgue values before Fubini, polar integration or passage to improper limits; real and imaginary test components are treated separately.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The uniformly charged ball of radius $a$ and total charge $Q$ in vacuum: the candidate piecewise field and continuous potential, the pointwise and distributional static equations with the piecewise-constant density and zero surface charge, the exterior Coulomb field of total charge $Q$, the vanishing jump of the normal field, and the finite energy $3Q^2/(20\pi\varepsilon_0a)$ equal to the assembly integral. The density is only piecewise continuous; no uniqueness, empirical or stability claim is made.
