consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the surface and integral interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v)$ be the conductor geometry of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with $\Omega_v$ connected and with the **outer boundary $\partial\Omega$ grounded**: the data on $\partial\Omega$ are the constant Dirichlet datum $0$; let $\rho_v\equiv0$ on $\Omega_v$ (the pure capacitor configuration: no volume source), and let the framework constants be those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. For each $j\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ let $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be the unit-potential solution of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) with the smooth data
$$\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$$
so that $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ on $\Omega_v$ with the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and let $\nu$ be the outward normal of $\Omega_v$ (so on $\partial D_j$ the normal $\nu$ points into the conductor). Define the **capacitance matrix** by
$$C_{jk}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi_k}{\partial\nu}\,dS,\qquad j,k=1,\dots,m,$$
the flux integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ (normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]) ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]). Then:
(a) [Linearity and matrix form] for every $V=(V_1,\dots,V_m)\in\mathbb R^m$ the unique equilibrium potential with conductor potentials $V$ and grounded outer boundary is $\varphi^V=\sum_{j=1}^mV_j\varphi_j$, and the conductor charges of [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d) are
$$Q_j(V)=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi^V}{\partial\nu}\,dS=\sum_{k=1}^mC_{jk}V_k,\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad Q=CV.$$
(b) [Reciprocity] $C$ is symmetric: $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ for all $j,k$; the symmetry is Green's symmetric pairing of the harmonic potentials $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$.
(c) [Energy identity] the field energy of the configuration is
$$U(V)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12V^{T}CV=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^mV_jQ_j(V),$$
and $U(V)>0$ for every $V\ne0$: $C$ is symmetric positive definite. In particular $U(V)\ge0$, with equality exactly for $V=0$, so every nonzero conductor-potential data set stores positive field energy.
(d) [Two-conductor reading] with only conductor $1$ driven and every other conductor grounded, $V=te_1$: $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $Q_j=C_{j1}t$ for $j\ne1$, and $U=\tfrac12C_{11}t^2=\tfrac12Q_1V_1=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; the **capacitance of the arrangement** at conductor $1$ with respect to the grounded reference is the positive geometric number $C_{11}=Q_1/V_1>0$, and the energy identities $U=\tfrac12QV=Q^2/(2C)=\tfrac12CV^2$ hold with $C=C_{11}$, $Q=Q_1$, $V=V_1$. By (c) the positivity holds for every diagonal entry, $C_{jj}>0$.
(e) [Assembly reading] by the quasi-static bookkeeping of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]](b), here applied to the surface charges of the conductors rather than to a volume density, $U$ is the external assembly work $\tfrac12\sum_jV_jQ_j$ of bringing the conductor charges to their places at fixed potentials with the grounded reference; the family $\varphi^V=s\varphi^V$, $0\le s\le1$ is an accounting prescription, not an asserted time-dependent Maxwell solution.
(f) [Scope] the theorem assumes: the smooth conductor geometry and connected vacuum region of the model, the grounded outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, zero volume source, and the existence and uniqueness of the unit-potential Dirichlet solutions ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c), [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a)). It asserts no solvability for arbitrary boundary data (the existence theorem is used only for the constant data above), no prescribed-total-charge problem, no dielectric or material response, no finite-conductivity or transient charging dynamics, no radiation, and no measurement; the matrix $C$ is a geometric object of the ideal electrostatic model, and the ideal parallel-plate and similar formulas are statements about this model only.

Existence of each $\varphi_j$: the pure electrostatic regime is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]; the datum that is $\delta_{jk}$ on $\partial D_k$ and $0$ on $\partial\Omega$ is constant, hence smooth, on each compact boundary piece of the disjoint union $\partial\Omega_v$, so [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) gives $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ and those boundary values. (b) Green's first identity on the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega_v$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], applied twice and subtracted) gives, for the harmonic $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$,
$$0=\int_{\Omega_v} igl(\varphi_j\Delta\varphi_k-\varphi_k\Delta\varphi_j igr)d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v} igl(\varphi_j\partial_
u\varphi_k-\varphi_k\partial_

$$\int_{\Omega_v} igl(\varphi^V\Delta\varphi^V+|

The Laplacian term vanishes, the outer boundary contributes $0$, and on $\partial D_j$ the trace of $\varphi^V$ is the constant $V_j$, so the boundary integral equals $\sum_jV_j\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_
u\varphi^VdS=\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)/\varepsilon_0$ by [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d); multiplying by $\varepsilon_0/2$ gives $U(V)=	frac12V^TCV$. Positivity: $

Thus $C$ is positive definite and in particular symmetric with positive diagonal. (d) is the case $V=te_1$ of (a) and (c): $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $U=	frac12C_{11}t^2=	frac12Q_1V_1$, and eliminating $t=Q_1/C_{11}$ gives $U=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; $C_{11}>0$ is (c) with $V=e_1$. (f) lists the hypotheses: only constant boundary data are solved, so no claim of arbitrary-boundary solvability or of charge-data solvability is made, and no material, radiative or empirical content is introduced.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the integral and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). **Declare the ideal parallel-plate model** of two infinite parallel charged planes in vacuo, read as equipotential ideal conductor surfaces of the same equilibrium structure as [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] (the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]): for a separation parameter $d>0$, half-separation $h=d/2$, a surface-density parameter $\sigma>0$ (C m$^{-2}$) and the framework constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the model consists of the field
$$E(x):=\begin{cases}-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}e_3,&|x_3|<h,\\[2pt]0,&|x_3|>h,\end{cases}\qquad x=(x_1,x_2,x_3),$$
together with the plane densities $+\sigma$ on $\Pi_+:=\{x_3=h\}$ and $-\sigma$ on $\Pi_-:=\{x_3=-h\}$, and with the piecewise potential $\varphi(x):=-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}x_3$ for $|x_3|\le h$, $\varphi:=-\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\ge h$ and $\varphi:=+\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\le-h$. Then:
(a) [Direct distributional verification] $E$ and $\varphi$ are locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $\Pi_+\cup\Pi_-$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there, $\varphi$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$ and constant on each plane with the values $\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=-\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$, $\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=+\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$; and in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$
$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\bigl(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,$$
where $\delta_{\Pi_\pm}(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\psi(x_1,x_2,\pm h)\,dx_1\,dx_2$ for compactly supported smooth $\psi$ are the plane distributions defined by the iterated Lebesgue integrals. Equivalently, the model realises the static electrostatic equations with the declared pair of plane densities and no other source, and the potential differences read off $\varphi$ are $\varphi(-h)-\varphi(h)=2\sigma h/\varepsilon_0=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(b) [Uniform field and voltage] the field between the planes has constant magnitude $|E|=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and is normal to the planes, and the potential difference between the plates is $V:=\varphi|_{\Pi_-}-\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(c) [Charge, capacitance and energy of the ideal model] for any chosen finite area $A>0$ the charge on the portion of area $A$ of the positive plate is $Q:=\sigma A$, so $Q=(\varepsilon_0A/d)V$ with the geometric ratio
$$C:=\frac QV=\frac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}>0,$$
independent of $\sigma$ and $V$; and the field energy contained in the slab of area $A$ between the plates is
$$U=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\text{slab of area }A}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2 .$$
(d) [Relation to the bounded-conductor theorem and scope] the linearity $Q=CV$, the positivity $C>0$ and the energy identities $U=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2$ are exactly the conclusions that [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]] proves for bounded conductor configurations with prescribed potentials and a grounded reference; this example verifies them directly for the ideal model because the infinite planes and the unbounded declared field are outside that theorem's hypotheses (compact conductors in a bounded vacuum region) and outside the declared stationary-sheet source type of [[def-em-weak-sources]], exactly as the ideal line source lies outside the compact-source types of the electrostatic page. No approximation theorem from finite plates to the infinite model is asserted; for a finite real plate pair the uniform-field model neglects the fringing field near the edges, which is not computed here, and the idealisation also omits the finite-thickness, material, transient and measurement content of any real capacitor.
consumer_reviews.strategy: All identities are computed directly from the explicit piecewise formulas; no compact-sheet jump theorem is invoked, because the planes are noncompact and the model is a declared idealization. (a) Local integrability is immediate from the boundedness of the piecewise field and the finiteness of the slab's intersections with compact sets ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]); the identification with regular distributions is [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. For a compactly supported smooth test $\psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=-\int E\cdot\nabla\psi=-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{|x_3|<h}\partial_3\psi\,d\lambda_3$ (inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and norm of [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]); Fubini ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]) writes the slab integral as $\int_{\mathbb R^2}\bigl(\int_{-h}^{h}\partial_3\psi(x_1,x_2,s)\,ds\bigr)dx_1dx_2$, and the inner integral is $\psi(x_1,x_2,h)-\psi(x_1,x_2,-h)$ by [[thm-integration-by-parts]] (the one-dimensional Newton-Leibniz identity, applicable because $\psi$ is smooth and compactly supported and the interval is bounded); hence $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-})(\psi)$, proving the divergence identity with the sign convention of [[def-distributional-derivative]] and [[def-distribution]]. The curl identity: $E_1=E_2=0$ and $E_3=-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\mathbf 1_{\{|x_3|<h\}}$ is a function of $x_3$ alone, so its distributional $x_1$- and $x_2$-derivatives vanish identically ([[def-distributional-derivative]]); hence $\operatorname{curl}E=(\partial_2E_3-\partial_3E_2,\partial_3E_1-\partial_1E_3,\partial_1E_2-\partial_2E_1)=0$. The potential formulas give $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on the three open regions ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and continuity across the planes is the equality of the two one-sided constants. (b) is the explicit evaluation, and (c) is arithmetic with the slab integral computed by Fubini: $\int_{\text{slab}}|E|^2=\frac{\sigma^2}{\varepsilon_0^2}Ad$. (d) states the exact relation to [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]]: that theorem's structure (linearity in the voltage, positive capacitance, energy equal to half the pairing $QV$) is what the computation reproduces, but its hypotheses (bounded conductor bodies, bounded vacuum region, Dirichlet solvability) are not met by the infinite-plane idealization, so the identities are verified here directly and the theorem is not applied; the fringing qualification is the ideal-model warning recorded by the design's X2 verification, recorded as scope rather than computed. No empirical content, no measurement and no claim about real capacitors beyond the stated approximation are made.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The ideal two-infinite-plane capacitor model in a named inertial frame: uniform field between the plates, zero field outside, plane charge densities +/- sigma, potential difference V = sigma d/epsilon_0, and the ideal-model charge-voltage and energy relations Q = (epsilon_0 A/d) V and U = Q^2/(2C) = CV^2/2 for a chosen area A. The infinite planes and unbounded field are declared idealizations outside the compact-conductor and declared-sheet-source hypotheses; the item asserts no fringe computation, no finite-geometry approximation theorem, no material or transient effect and no measurement.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$) that is either closed ($\gamma(0)=\gamma(L)$ with matching one-sided derivatives) or a wire segment with free endpoints, let $I\in\mathbb R$, let $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds$ be the finite Riemann source moment defined by this displayed integral in the closed case. For an embedded closed loop this agrees with [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b); embeddedness is not required for the present parametrized-curve calculation. Let $B$ be a prescribed external magnetic field, of class $C^0$ on a neighbourhood of the trace of $\gamma$ in part (a) and of class $C^2$ on an open set containing the closed ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ in parts (b)-(d). Adopt the thin-wire coupling hypothesis (W): for a general closed parametrized curve use the stated direct neutral-wire Riemann coupling (with multiplicity of traversal retained); in the embedded closed-loop specialization its source interpretation is exactly [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1); for an open curve use a compact segment of a fed or closed neutral circuit, including a segment of the declared infinite wire of (c2). Adopt separately for that parametrized wire or local segment the direct external magnetic coupling $dF=I\,d\gamma\times B$ and $dN=\gamma\times dF$, as an ideal extension motivated by the smooth continuum Lorentz law [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii); that smooth-source postulate does not itself include singular currents. An isolated static neutral open segment is not asserted: its standalone current satisfies $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm seg}=I(\delta_{\gamma(0)}-\delta_{\gamma(L)})$, so its endpoint feed/return cannot be suppressed in a global model. Force and torque here concern only the specified local segment under this adopted coupling. Then:

(a) [Force and torque under (W)]

$$F:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad N:=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\bigl(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\bigr)\,ds,$$

the componentwise Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the compact interval $[0,L]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]).

(b) [Constant field] If $\gamma$ is closed and $B$ is constant on a neighbourhood of the loop, then $F=0$ and $N=m\times B$ exactly.

(c) [Slowly varying field] Let $\gamma$ be closed with $|\gamma(s)|\le a$ for all $s$, let $B$ be $C^2$ on an open set containing $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with constants $M_1,M_2$ such that $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ and $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|,|y|\le a$, and suppose $\operatorname{div}B=0$ on $B_a(0)$ (as holds for the external part of any smooth-branch vacuum field by [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Then

$$F=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)+R_F,\qquad N=m\times B(0)+R_N,$$

with $|R_F|\le\frac12|I|\,L\,a^2M_2$ and $|R_N|\le|I|\,L\,a^2M_1$, where $\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)$ is the gradient at $0$ of $x\mapsto m\cdot B(x)$ for the fixed vector $m$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

(d) [Sufficient condition] If the external field is the magnetostatic field of a compact smooth steady current $J_{\rm ext}\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm ext}=0$ ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], [[pthm-em-biot-savart]]), then it is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and meets the hypotheses of (c) on every ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with finite constants $M_1,M_2$.

(e) [Scope] Only the external field acts on the loop: the loop's own field, self-force, radiation reaction, mechanical support and material response are outside the statement, and no claim is made about the loop's dynamics, deformation or failure. The coupling (W) is an explicit idealisation of a neutral thin wire at rest in the laboratory frame; it is adopted, not derived, and the theorem is conditional on it. No measurement or uncertainty is involved. Parts (a)-(c), conditional on the explicit coupling (W) and the supplied curve and external field, are finite Riemann-integral calculations and use no Choice axiom. Part (d), transporting the Newtonian-potential construction, assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).
consumer_reviews.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct evaluation of the pairings under the coupling, the antisymmetric first-moment identities for a closed curve, one Taylor expansion with an explicit remainder, and the compact-current sufficient condition. 1.1 (a) Under the separately adopted coupling (W), integrate the continuous external force along the compact curve directly in the Riemann sense: $F=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds$, and taking moments gives $N=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s)))\,ds$; both integrands are continuous on $[0,L]$ because $\gamma,\gamma'$ and $B\circ\gamma$ are ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). 1.2 (b) For constant $B$, $F=I(\int_0^L\gamma'\,ds)\times B=0$ because $\gamma(L)=\gamma(0)$. For the torque, $\gamma\times(\gamma'\times B)=\gamma'(\gamma\cdot B)-B(\gamma\cdot\gamma')$, so with $M_{jl}:=\int_0^L\gamma_j\gamma'_l\,ds$, $$N=I\int_0^L(\gamma\cdot B)\gamma'\,ds-I B\int_0^L\gamma\cdot\gamma'\,ds=I B_jM_{jl}e_l .$$ The second integral vanishes because $\gamma\cdot\gamma'=\frac12\frac{d}{ds}|\gamma|^2$ integrates to $0$ over a closed curve. For the first, integrating $\frac{d}{ds}(\gamma_j\gamma_l)=0$ over the closed curve gives $M_{jl}+M_{lj}=0$; for such an antisymmetric matrix the moment relation $m_p=\frac I2\varepsilon_{pab}M_{ab}$ is equivalent to $I M_{jl}=\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p$, and substituting this into $I B_jM_{jl}e_l$ and using $B_j\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p e_l=m\times B$ gives $N=m\times B$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

2.1 (c) Write $B(x)=B(0)+DB(0)x+R(x)$ with $|R(x)|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|\le a$; this is the quantitative second-order Taylor hypothesis, the case $k=1$ of [[thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder]] applied componentwise, with the bound on the Lagrange term supplied by the stated $M_2$. Splitting the force of (a), the constant term vanishes as in (b); the linear term is $I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i$ and, with $I M_{lj}=\varepsilon_{ljp}m_p$, the contraction $\varepsilon_{ijk}\varepsilon_{ljp}=\delta_{kp}\delta_{il}-\delta_{kl}\delta_{ip}$ yields $$I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i=\bigl(\partial_i(m\cdot B)(0)-m_i\operatorname{div}B(0)\bigr)e_i=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0),$$ using $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$; the remainder obeys $|I\int_0^L\gamma'\times R\,ds|\le|I|L\sup_{|x|\le a}|R(x)|\le\frac12|I|La^2M_2$ ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). For the torque, step 1.2 gives $N=m\times B(0)+I\int_0^L\gamma\times(\gamma'\times(B(\gamma)-B(0)))\,ds$, and the remainder is bounded by $|I|\int_0^L|\gamma||\gamma'||B(\gamma)-B(0)|\,ds\le|I|\,a\cdot1\cdot M_1a\cdot L$. This proves (c).

2.2 (d) By [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] the external field of a compact smooth conserved current is $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $A$ of class $C^\infty$, hence $B\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}B=0$; on a bounded ball the suprema of $|DB|$ and $|D^2B|$ are finite, and the mean-value and second-order Taylor estimates provide the constants $M_1,M_2$ of (c). 2.3 (e) records that (W) is a declared idealisation: only the external field acts, and no self-field, matter model or dynamics enters. Countable Choice is inherited in part (d) through the Newtonian suppliers; parts (a)-(c) use the stated finite Riemann coupling directly and are choice-free. The moment identity follows by contracting two alternating symbols and uses no division by $I$; for $I=0$ the moment, force, torque and both remainders are zero. No scalar distribution action $\langle J,B\rangle$ is equated with a vector force, and continuity rather than smoothness of the external field suffices for the adopted compact-curve Riemann coupling. For an open segment the scalar divergence test gives $-I\int_0^L\frac{d}{ds}\varphi(\gamma(s))ds=I(\varphi(\gamma(0))-\varphi(\gamma(L)))$, the stated endpoint identity. The force/moment algebra applies to all the stated closed parametrized $C^2$ curves, including self-intersecting or multiply traversed curves: closure, unit-speed parametrization and the explicit finite moment integral suffice. Only the embedded closed specialization invokes the ideal-loop source object of the preceding definition.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: Force and torque on a declared ideal thin-wire loop in a prescribed external magnetic field, under an explicitly adopted neutral-wire Lorentz coupling. Only the external field acts: self-fields, radiation reaction, mechanical support, deformation and material failure are outside the statement; no dynamics, radiation or empirical measurement is claimed, and the result is conditional on the adopted coupling (W).

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $d>0$ and $I_1,I_2\in\mathbb R$; let wire 1 be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I_1$ along the third coordinate axis and wire 2 the translate of that ideal line current by $d\,e_1$, of amplitude $I_2$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and adopt for the force on wire 2 the thin-wire coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]], restricted to the external field of wire 1. Then the force per unit length on wire 2 is

$$\mathbf f=\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_3\times e_2=-\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_1,$$

i.e. attraction towards wire 1 (direction $-e_1$) for currents in the same direction ($I_1I_2>0$), repulsion for opposite directions, and magnitude $\mu_0|I_1I_2|/(2\pi d)$ per unit length. The comparison uses only the external field of wire 1 at the position of wire 2; the self-fields and the mechanical support forces of the two infinite wires are excluded, no claim is made about the total force on either infinite wire, and no measurement is involved.
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Verification.** Wire 1 has the admitted field $B_1=\mu_0I_1/(2\pi\rho)\,e_\varphi$ of [[ex-em-infinite-wire-and-solenoid]](a), which at the points $(d,0,x_3)$ of wire 2 takes the constant value $B_1=\frac{\mu_0I_1}{2\pi d}\,e_2$ (there $e_\varphi=e_2$). By the coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]](a) applied to the compact straight segments $\{(d,0,x_3):|x_3|\le S\}$ of wire 2 (with arc-length parameter $x_3$ and $|\gamma'|=1$), the force on the segment is $$I_2\int_{-S}^{S}e_3\times B_1\,dx_3=2S\,\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,(e_3\times e_2),$$ the Riemann integral of a constant continuous integrand over a compact interval ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Dividing by the length $2S$ gives the force per unit length of the displayed form, independent of $S$; the sign of $I_1I_2$ gives attraction or repulsion as stated. Only the external field of wire 1 is used, and the self-field of wire 2 and the support forces of both infinite wires are excluded; the computation is a local external-force comparison, not a solution of the two-wire dynamics, and involves no measurement. The preceding same-B-page example is a permitted intra-page supplier and its corrected proof uses the A-level ideal-line lemma and explicit model adoption. The compact segment uses the separately adopted local coupling, with the return/feed outside the force segment; no isolated neutral open segment is claimed to be globally conserved. Countable Choice is inherited by the asserted ideal-line model, while the final constant-force Riemann calculation is finite.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: A local external-force comparison between two declared ideal parallel straight wires, restricted to the force per unit length that wire 1's external field exerts on wire 2 under the adopted neutral-thin-wire coupling. Self-fields and support forces of infinitely long wires are excluded; no dynamics, circuit model, material response or measurement is claimed.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the jointly $C^1$ fields $E,B$ of [[def-em-fields]], the continuous sources $\rho,J$ of [[def-em-sources]], the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the force density $f:=\rho E+J\times B$ of that clause (ii), in $\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the momentum density $g$, Maxwell stress $\sigma$ and momentum flux $\Pi=-\sigma$ of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]].
(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-f,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f,$$
componentwise $\partial_tg_i-\sum_j\partial_j\sigma_{ij}=-(\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i)$.
(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with $\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let $t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $n$ be the outward unit normal. Then for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and each $i$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}g_i\,dx=\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_j\sigma_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}f_i\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_j\Pi_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}f_i\,dx.$$
(c) [Scope] The identities are conditional on the two adopted postulates. The force density $f$ is defined only for the matter model of clause (ii), so no claim is made about a prescribed current without such a matter model. No conservation of the total momentum follows unless the boundary term vanishes or is included in the chosen system. The weak branch, singular sources and non-integrable products are excluded as in [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]; no self-force, radiation reaction or magnetic-monopole coupling is included, in accordance with the exclusions of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]. This is not an empirical claim.
consumer_reviews.strategy:
**Proof technique:** componentwise computation from the quadratic stress identity for (a); the parameter-integral lemma and the divergence theorem for (b). (a): [[lem-em-quadratic-stress-identity]] applied to $F=E$ with coefficient $\varepsilon_0$ and to $F=B$ with coefficient $\mu_0^{-1}$ gives
$$\operatorname{div}\sigma=\varepsilon_0\bigl(E\operatorname{div}E-E\times\operatorname{curl}E\bigr)+\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(B\operatorname{div}B-B\times\operatorname{curl}B\bigr).$$
Substituting the smooth-branch equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ gives $\operatorname{div}\sigma=\rho E+\varepsilon_0E\times\partial_tB-B\times J-\varepsilon_0B\times\partial_tE$, where $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] converts the last term. The product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] with the component form of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $\partial_tg=\varepsilon_0\partial_t(E\times B)=\varepsilon_0(\partial_tE\times B+E\times\partial_tB)$, so the four remaining terms combine into $\operatorname{div}\sigma=f+\partial_tg$, using $-B\times J=J\times B$ and $\partial_tE\times B=-B\times\partial_tE$; this is (a). (b): for each $i$, [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates $t\mapsto\int_{\Omega'}g_i$ under the integral sign on the compact set $\overline{\Omega'}$ (the integrands $g_i$ and $\partial_tg_i$ are continuous), and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies to the $C^1$ vector field $(\sigma_{i1},\sigma_{i2},\sigma_{i3})$ on $\Omega'$; the second display follows from $\Pi=-\sigma$. Clause (c) records the hypotheses and exclusions; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only through the divergence theorem, and no empirical premise is used.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The conditional local and fixed-volume momentum balance $\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-f$ (equivalently $\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f$) for the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate and the Lorentz force density $f=\rho E+J\times B$ of the continuum coupling clause, on bounded piecewise $C^1$ domains under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in the fixed-volume form. Excluded: the weak branch, singular sources and non-integrable products, matter models other than clause (ii), self-force, radiation reaction and magnetic monopoles; no conservation without vanishing or included boundary flux; no empirical claim.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], the jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]], continuous sources, and the force density $f=\rho E+J\times B$), and let $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$, the orbital angular momentum density $\ell=x\times g$ and its flux $x\times\Pi$ be those of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] relative to the origin fixed there.
(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_t\ell+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)=-x\times f,$$
componentwise $\partial_t\ell_i+\sum_j\partial_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}=-(x\times f)_i$, where $\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)_i:=\sum_j\partial_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}$ and $(x\times f)_i=\sum_{j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}x_jf_k$ with the Levi-Civita symbol of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]].
(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Under the domain, time-interval and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b), and with $n$ the outward unit normal, for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and each $i$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}\ell_i\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}(x\times f)_i\,dx.$$
(c) [Scope] The identities depend on the origin fixed in [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]](e) through the explicit factor $x$; no conservation of angular momentum follows unless the boundary flux vanishes or is included in the chosen system. The hypotheses and exclusions of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](c) are inherited. The density $\ell$ is orbital, $\ell=x\times g$; no spin or intrinsic angular momentum of matter is defined or claimed by this item. This is not an empirical claim.
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Proof technique:** apply the second part of [[lem-em-quadratic-stress-identity]] to the momentum balance and integrate. The local identity is exactly the general angular identity of that lemma: its hypothesis is $\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f$ with $\Pi$ symmetric, the first part is [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](a) in the form $\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f$, and the symmetry $\Pi_{ij}=\Pi_{ji}$ holds because $\sigma$ is symmetric by [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]](b) and $\Pi=-\sigma$. The lemma then gives $\partial_t(x\times g)+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)=-x\times f$ with $(x\times\Pi)_{i\ell}=\sum_{j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}x_j\Pi_{k\ell}$, which is display (a). For (b), [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates each component $t\mapsto\int_{\Omega'}\ell_i$ under the integral sign and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies to the vector field $\bigl((x\times\Pi)_{i1},(x\times\Pi)_{i2},(x\times\Pi)_{i3}\bigr)$ on $\Omega'$; its components are $C^1$ because $x$ is smooth and $\Pi$ is built from $C^1$ fields. Clause (c) records origin dependence, the inherited hypotheses, and the absence of any spin or intrinsic contribution; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only through the divergence theorem and no empirical premise is used.

Orbital density $x\times g$ only: no spin, intrinsic matter angular momentum, singular sources or weak-branch fields; no conservation without vanishing or included boundary flux; no empirical claim.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the Lebesgue and polar interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $q\in\mathbb R$, $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $E_q$ be the ideal point-charge field of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d) ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). For $0<\delta<R$ put
$$U_q(\delta,R):=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\{\delta\le|x-x_0|\le R\}}|E_q(x)|^2\,d\lambda_3(x)$$
(the truncated field energy of the shell between the two spheres, [[def-metric-ball]]). Then:
(a) [Exact truncated energy] for all $0<\delta<R$,
$$U_q(\delta,R)=\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0}\Bigl(\frac1\delta-\frac1R\Bigr);$$
(b) [Divergence] $\lim_{R\to\infty}U_q(\delta,R)=q^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0\delta)$ for every $\delta>0$, and for $q\ne0$
$$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}U_q(\delta,R)=+\infty\qquad\text{for every }R>0;$$
so the field energy of the ideal point charge is locally infinite at its own location, and any finite-energy treatment of a point-like charge must modify the source/field near the singularity or introduce an explicit cutoff;
(c) [Limits of the mass inference] the identity is a divergence of the *field energy of the idealised point source* in the framework's SI conventions. It does not assert that a physical particle has infinite rest mass, does not identify field energy with rest mass, contains no measurement, and involves neither a self-force nor a contradiction claim for classical electrodynamics: the framework supplies no mass-energy identification for a charged particle, and the smooth compact-source field/assembly energy of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] remains finite. The compact $L^1$ branch of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] retains its locally integrable potential and distributional Poisson equation; it does not guarantee finite field energy for arbitrary $L^1$ densities. The point source itself is the idealisation of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)); its energy divergence is a mathematical property of that idealisation, not an empirical result.
consumer_reviews.strategy:
For (a), $|E_q(x)|=|q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|^2)$ for $x\ne x_0$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d), [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]), so $|E_q|^2=q^2/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2|x-x_0|^4)$ and by the polar formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] with the unit-sphere measure of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ from [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]] and [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]; the integrand is nonnegative and Borel, [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]])
$$\int_{\delta\le|x-x_0|\le R}|E_q|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac{q^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2}\cdot 4\pi\int_\delta^R r^{-2}\,dr=\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2}\Bigl(\frac1\delta-\frac1R\Bigr),$$
where the one-dimensional integral is evaluated by the fundamental theorem and the derivative of $r\mapsto-1/r$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]); multiplying by $\varepsilon_0/2$ gives (a) ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). For (b), let $R\to\infty$ in (a) for fixed $\delta$ (the left-hand integral increases to the exterior integral by monotone convergence, [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], giving the first limit) and let $\delta\downarrow0$ for fixed $R$: $1/\delta\to\infty$ for $q\ne0$ (directly from the explicit formula and the order properties of the reals), so the truncated energies tend to $+\infty$. Any neighbourhood of $x_0$ therefore contains field energy exceeding any prescribed bound. For (c): the computation uses only the idealised point-source field of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d); it makes no use of, and does not assert, a mass-energy relation for a charged particle, a self-force, a regularisation or any measurement ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]); the contrast with the finite energies of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] is the contrast between an extended compactly supported source and the point idealisation. No claims about the field at $x_0$ itself are made: the truncated integrals avoid the singularity ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]). The choice cost is the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the Lebesgue/polar interface. Finite-interval integrations of the continuous one-variable test/radial integrands above use [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] to identify their Riemann/FTC values with their Lebesgue values before Fubini, polar integration or passage to improper limits; real and imaginary test components are treated separately.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The truncated electric field energy of the idealised point charge in vacuum: the shell energy is $q^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0)(1/\delta-1/R)$, finite for $0<\delta<R$ but divergent as the inner cutoff $\delta\downarrow0$ for $q\ne0$. The item records this divergence as a property of the point idealisation and explicitly excludes inferences about particle rest mass, self-force, empirical measurement or inconsistency of the framework; finite-energy statements remain those of the compact-source branches.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the jointly $C^1$ fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of [[def-em-fields]] (so the additional derivatives required by each displayed Maxwell equation exist and are continuous), the continuous source fields $\rho,J$ of [[def-em-sources]], the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and the energy density $u$ and Poynting vector $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]].
(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E,$$
where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] taken at fixed $t$ and $\partial_t$ the partial derivative at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].
(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with $\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let $t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, and let $n$ be the outward unit normal of $\partial\Omega'$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the hypothesis under which that divergence theorem is stated. Then for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}u(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\Omega'}J\cdot E\,dx-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}S\cdot n\,dS.$$
(c) [Interpretation and scope] Under clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], $J\cdot E$ is the power density supplied to the matter model of that coupling, so the two identities read as a local, respectively fixed-volume, energy balance of the field and that matter model. Nothing is claimed for a prescribed current without such a matter model, for the weak branch of the Maxwell postulate, for singular sources, or at field points where the products defining $u$ or $S$ are not locally integrable; the fixed-volume identity retains its boundary term and asserts no conservation unless that term vanishes or is included in the chosen system. The theorem is a conditional consequence of the adopted postulates and is not an empirical claim.
consumer_reviews.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct componentwise computation for (a); the parameter-integral lemma and the divergence theorem for (b). (a): the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], read componentwise) gives $\partial_tu=\varepsilon_0\langle E,\partial_tE\rangle+\mu_0^{-1}\langle B,\partial_tB\rangle$ with the inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Substituting Faraday's law $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and the Ampere-Maxwell law in the form $\mu_0^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B=\varepsilon_0\partial_tE+J$ (using $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]]) gives
$$\partial_tu=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(\langle E,\operatorname{curl}B\rangle-\langle B,\operatorname{curl}E\rangle\bigr)-E\cdot J=-\mu_0^{-1}\operatorname{div}(E\times B)-J\cdot E,$$
where the last step is the cross-product divergence identity $\operatorname{div}(E\times B)=\langle\operatorname{curl}E,B\rangle-\langle E,\operatorname{curl}B\rangle$ of [[lem-the-divergence-and-curl-of-a-cross-product]]; since $S=\mu_0^{-1}E\times B$, this is the asserted display. (b): fix $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and choose $t_0<t_0'<t<t_1'<t_1$. The maps $u$ and $\partial_tu$ are continuous on the compact set $\overline{\Omega'}\times[t_0',t_1']$, so [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] applied to the compact measurable $\overline{\Omega'}$ permits differentiation under the integral sign; then [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], whose hypotheses (finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation, $C^1$ field on the closure, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) are met by $S$ on $\Omega'$, converts $\int_{\Omega'}\operatorname{div}S$ into the boundary flux; $J\cdot E$ is continuous and hence integrable on $\overline{\Omega'}$. Clause (c) records the interpretation under [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] and the exclusions of the weak branch, singular sources and non-integrable products; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only through the divergence theorem, and no empirical premise is used.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The conditional local and fixed-volume electromagnetic energy balance $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ under the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell postulate, in a named inertial chart with SI constants, and its fixed-volume integrated form on bounded piecewise $C^1$ domains under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The work interpretation of $J\cdot E$ is conditional on clause (ii) of the Lorentz-coupling postulate. Excluded: the weak branch, singular sources and non-integrable quadratic products; no conservation without vanishing or included boundary flux; no empirical claim.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$, $E_0>0$, and on $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$, the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],
$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$
The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the direction $e_3$ ('crossed' fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$, $B$ along $e_2$. Then:
(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.
(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$
and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box $B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B}u\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is parallel to $e_3$, and the upper face $z=b$ has outward flux $L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and the lower face $z=a$ has outward flux $-L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$. Their respective signed contributions to the field-energy change are $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.
(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave, the finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example asserts nothing about the total energy of the field over all of $\mathbb R^3$ nor any empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared parameters of the configuration.
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, with the oscillatory derivatives computed through the complex-exponential encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. (a): the fields are of class $C^\infty$ because they are real parts of compositions of the linear map $(x,t)\mapsto i(kz-\omega t)$ with the entire exponential and of the real-linear projection, so the smooth calculus applies ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]); in particular, the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $\exp\circ(i(kz-\omega t))$, with the real total differentiability and derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]) and Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]), gives $\partial_te^{i\theta}=-i\omega e^{i\theta}$, $\partial_ze^{i\theta}=ike^{i\theta}$ and, taking real parts, $\partial_t\cos\theta=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_z\cos\theta=-k\sin\theta$; substitution into the four smooth-branch equations verifies them with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ (both divergences vanish because the fields depend only on $z$ and have no $e_3$ component, curl $E=-\partial_tB$ and curl $B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ reduce to the displayed scalar identities using $\omega=ck$). (b): $(E\times B)_3=\lvert E\rvert\lvert B\rvert=E_0^2c^{-1}\cos^2\theta$ by the orthogonal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and $\lvert E\rvert^2=E_0^2\cos^2\theta$, $\lvert B\rvert^2=E_0^2c^{-2}\cos^2\theta$; with $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ and $1/(\mu_0c)=\varepsilon_0c$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] this gives the displayed $u$ and $S$; the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_tu=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\omega\cos\theta\sin\theta$ and $\partial_zS_3=-2\varepsilon_0cE_0^2k\cos\theta\sin\theta$, whose sum vanishes because $\omega=ck$; this is the local identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] for $J=0$. (c): $u$ is continuous and independent of $(x,y)$, so [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] reduces $\int_Bu\,dV$ to $L_1L_2\int_a^bu(z,t)\,dz$; [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates that integral under the integral sign; the local identity and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=-L_1L_2\int_a^b\partial_zS_3\,dz=-L_1L_2(S_3(b,t)-S_3(a,t))$; the evaluation of the six face integrals uses only that $S=S_3e_3$ is independent of $(x,y)$. (d) records the scope; no empirical premise is used.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The explicit ideal source-free travelling plane-wave configuration $E=E_0\cos(kz-\omega t)e_1$, $B=(E_0/c)\cos(kz-\omega t)e_2$, $\omega=ck$, as a worked example of the vacuum energy density and Poynting vector and of the local and finite-box energy accounting of the electromagnetic energy balance. The example asserts nothing about the total energy over all space and no empirical realization; all quantities are the idealised fields of the adopted framework.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]; jointly $C^1$ fields; continuous sources), and suppose in addition that matter fields $u_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $S_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, $g_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and a symmetric $C^1$ tensor field $\Pi_m$ ($\Pi_{m,ij}=\Pi_{m,ji}$) are given on $\Omega\times I$ satisfying the matter balance equations
$$\partial_tu_m+\operatorname{div}S_m=J\cdot E,\qquad\partial_tg_m+\operatorname{div}\Pi_m=f,$$
where $f=\rho E+J\times B$ and $J\cdot E$ are the coupling densities of clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]. Put $u_{\mathrm{tot}}:=u+u_m$, $S_{\mathrm{tot}}:=S+S_m$, $g_{\mathrm{tot}}:=g+g_m$, $\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\Pi+\Pi_m$ (symmetric) and $\ell_{\mathrm{tot}}:=x\times g_{\mathrm{tot}}$, with the fields $u,S,g,\Pi$ of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]].
(a) [Local conservation] On $\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_tu_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0,\qquad\partial_tg_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}}=0,\qquad\partial_t\ell_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}})=0.$$
(b) [Fixed-volume conservation] Under the additional regularity and the domain, time-interval and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]](b) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b) for $(u_m,S_m)$ and $(g_m,\Pi_m)$, and with $n$ the outward unit normal, for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}u_{\mathrm{tot}}\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}S_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot n\,dS,\qquad\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}g_{\mathrm{tot},i}\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_j\Pi_{\mathrm{tot},ij}n_j\Bigr)dS,$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}\ell_{\mathrm{tot},i}\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_j(x\times\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}})_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS.$$
Thus the totals $\int_{\Omega'}u_{\mathrm{tot}}$, $\int_{\Omega'}g_{\mathrm{tot}}$ and $\int_{\Omega'}\ell_{\mathrm{tot}}$ are constant in $t$ exactly while the corresponding boundary fluxes vanish; in general the boundary fluxes must be included in the chosen system.
(c) [Scope] The matter balances are additional, explicitly stated assumptions, not consequences of the Maxwell postulates: a prescribed current $(\rho,J)$ does not by itself supply matter fields satisfying them, and 'closed system' is a modelling choice about which boundary terms are included. The hypotheses and exclusions of the two field theorems are inherited, and no empirical claim is made.
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Proof technique:** add the field identities to the assumed matter balances and integrate. (a): the local energy identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]](a), $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$, added to the assumed $\partial_tu_m+\operatorname{div}S_m=J\cdot E$ gives $\partial_tu_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$ by linearity of $\partial_t$ and $\operatorname{div}$ componentwise; the local momentum identity of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](a), $\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f$, added to the assumed $\partial_tg_m+\operatorname{div}\Pi_m=f$ gives the second line. For the angular line apply [[lem-em-quadratic-stress-identity]] to the matter pair: from $\partial_tg_m+\operatorname{div}\Pi_m=f$ with $\Pi_m$ symmetric it gives $\partial_t(x\times g_m)+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi_m)=x\times f$ (the lemma is applied to $g_m,\Pi_m$ with right-hand side $-f$), and [[pthm-em-angular-balance]](a) gives $\partial_t(x\times g)+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)=-x\times f$; adding cancels the torque density, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is symmetric as the sum of symmetric tensors. (b): apply [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] to each total density and flux exactly as in [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]](b), [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b) and [[pthm-em-angular-balance]](b); the displayed regularity of the matter fields makes every integrand $C^1$ on $\overline{\Omega'}\times[t_0',t_1']$. Clause (c) records that the matter balances are assumptions and that no isolated closed system is derived from Maxwell alone; no empirical premise and no choice beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: The conditional local and fixed-volume conservation of the total energy, momentum and orbital angular momentum of the electromagnetic field plus an explicitly assumed matter model whose balances $\partial_tu_m+\operatorname{div}S_m=J\cdot E$ and $\partial_tg_m+\operatorname{div}\Pi_m=f$ with symmetric $\Pi_m$ are given, under the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate, the continuum coupling clause and the same bounded-domain and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses as the field balances. The matter balances are assumptions, not derivations; no isolated closed system is derived from Maxwell alone; no empirical claim.

consumer_reviews.statement: Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value theorem to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$. (a) With $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]) and $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U_\nu=\gamma(-c,v)$: $q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(cF^i{}_0+F^i{}_jv^j\bigr)=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ since $F^i{}_0=\eta_{00}F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; and $q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. Since $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\Phi(U)^i$ and $d/dt=\gamma^{-1}d/d\tau$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)), $dp_i/dt=\gamma^{-1}\,q\gamma(E+v\times B)_i=q(E+v\times B)_i$ with $p=m\gamma v$ from [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a); the temporal component gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$ after multiplying by $c$. (b) $\eta(U,U)$ has derivative $2\eta(U,U')=2(q/m)\eta(U,\Phi(U))=0$ by the orthogonality clause of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] (which needs no derivative of the field); the initial value $-c^2$ is that of the four-velocity. For the stated solution-preservation conclusion, differentiability makes $U$ continuous and the norm identity gives $(U^0)^2=c^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2\ge c^2$. Thus $U^0$ cannot vanish; on a connected interval its sign cannot change by [[thm-intermediate-value]]. Positive initial $U^0$ therefore stays positive and the solution stays in the future timelike component. This conditional argument asserts no existence or continuation of solutions. (c) $z:=|v|^2/c^2$ and $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$; by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ with $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. At $z=0$ all stated differences and bounds are zero directly; henceforth assume $0<z\le\delta^2$. First-order bound by the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $|f(z)-1|=|f'(\xi)|z\le z\,/\,(2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2})$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, using monotonicity of the positive power ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]). Second-order remainder by Cauchy's mean value theorem ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]) applied on $[0,z]$ to $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac s2$ and $g(s):=s^2$: $q(z)/z^2=q'(\xi)/g'(\xi)=(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12)/(2\xi)$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, and the mean value theorem on $[0,\xi]$ applied to $f'$ gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in(0,\xi)$, so $|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2|=\tfrac12|f''(\eta)|z^2\le\tfrac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

Put $h:=qE_0/(mc)$, carrying the unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$, and for $r_0\in\mathbb R^3$ define the chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ by $$r(t):=r_0+ rac{c}{h} igl(\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}-1 igr)e_1\quad(h
e0),\qquad r(t):=r_0\quad(h=0),$$ $$v(t):=r'(t)= rac{c\,ht}{\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}}\,e_1\ (h
e0),\qquad \gamma(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2},\qquad p(t):=m\gamma(t)v(t).$$ Then: (i) [Exact solution] for $h

(ii) [Energy] $\gamma(t)mc^2=mc^2\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ and $ rac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$: the field delivers power $qE\cdot v$ to the particle. (iii) [Unscoped Newtonian extrapolation] For $h
e0$, the Newtonian constant-acceleration prediction $v_N(t):=(qE_0/m)t\,e_1$ satisfies $v(t)=v_N(t)/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$, so the two agree only to first order in $|ht|$ and $|v_N(t)|=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}\,|v(t)|$ exceeds $c$ for $|t|>1/|h|$, whereas the exact solution of the adopted coupling remains subluminal at every finite time; for this explicit solution the approximation is quantified directly. Put $r_N(t)=r_0+	frac12hc t^2e_1$. For $h
e0$, $$|v-v_N|\le rac c2|ht|^3,\qquad |r-r_N|\le rac{c}{8|h|}|ht|^4.$$ Thus on $|ht|\le\delta$ the velocity error is at most $c\delta^3/2$ and the displacement error at most $c\delta^4/(8|h|)$; these are special-model comparisons, not a general trajectory-stability consequence of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c). consumer_reviews.strategy: **Verification:** direct differentiation and substitution. For $h\ne0$ set $g(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$; by [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the map $t\mapsto(1+h^2t^2)^{1/2}$ is differentiable with $g'(t)=h^2t/g(t)$ ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]), hence $r'(t)=(c/h)g'(t)e_1=chte_1/g(t)=v(t)$ and $|v(t)|/c=|ht|/g(t)<1$ because $h^2t^2<1+h^2t^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]), with $|v(t)|\to c$ as $|t|\to\infty$. Then $p(t)=m\gamma(t)v(t)=mc\,ht\,e_1=qE_0t\,e_1$, so $dp/dt=qE_0e_1$, and $q(E+v\times B)=qE_0e_1$ since $B=0$ and $v\times0=0$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the power identity is $\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=mc^2h^2t/g(t)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$. The curve is future timelike: its tangent $(c,v(t))$ has $\eta$-square $-c^2+|v(t)|^2<0$ with positive time component, in the sense of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a) and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the vector-valued derivative is [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. Part (iii) is the displayed identity $v=v_N/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ with $v_N=(qE_0/m)te_1=hct\,e_1$, whose norm exceeds $c$ exactly when $|ht|>1$. For the direct error bounds let $s=ht$ and $g=\sqrt{1+s^2}\ge1$. Rationalization gives $g-1=s^2/(g+1)\le s^2/2$ and $1-g^{-1}=(g-1)/g\le s^2/2$. Since $v=v_N/g$ and $|v_N|=c|s|$, the velocity bound follows. Also $1+s^2/2-g=(g-1)^2/2\le s^4/8$, so multiplying its absolute value by $c/|h|$ gives the displacement bound. This directly proves the special-model approximation on the declared interval without importing a general stability claim. For $h=0$, $q=0$, $r=r_N=r_0$ and $v=v_N=0$, and every force/power identity is zero; no formula divides by $h$ in that branch. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.

consumer_reviews.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event $p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$, $F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then: (a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart, $$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$ equivalently, componentwise, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$. (a′) [Arbitrary boost direction] For a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v|<c$, use the actual vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]], with $\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along $\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$, including $v=0$, $$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$ At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is assigned.  (b) [Invariants] at every such $p$, $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$ equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in $x'$. (c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if $\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper orthochronous change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the arbitrary-direction boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\beta$, where $\beta$ is the vector parameter of that factorization. The axis-only law (a) is not substituted for a general vector boost. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation from the transformation law, then the scalar contractions. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (a′) For $v\ne0$ put $u=v/|v|$. Choose a coordinate vector $e_j$ not parallel to $u$, set $a=(e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u)/|e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u|$ and $b=u\times a$. Direct cross-product coordinates show $(u,a,b)$ is an oriented orthonormal basis. Let $R$ have these vectors as rows, so $Ru=e_1$, $R^{\mathsf T}R=I$ and $\det R=1$; only one finite choice is used. Substituting the matrix of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{-1}\Lambda_{|v|/c}\widehat R$. Apply the rotation component law proved in (c), then the axis computation (a), then rotate back. The determinant-one cofactor identity gives $R(p\times q)=(Rp)\times(Rq)$, yielding the parallel/perpendicular formulas. Use $\gamma_v-1=\gamma_v^2|v|^2/(c^2(\gamma_v+1))$ to combine the pieces into the displayed nonsingular vector formulas; at zero the separately defined boost is the identity.  (b) The two expressions are the two independent scalar contractions of the two-form; substituting the component law into $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ with $\eta'=\eta$ shows invariance, equivalently clauses (c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) identifies them with $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$. (c) For the rotation case $\Lambda^0{}_0=1$, $\Lambda^0{}_j=\Lambda^i{}_0=0$, $\Lambda^i{}_j=R^i{}_j$ give $F'^{0i}=R^i{}_jF^{0j}$ and $F'^{ij}=R^i{}_kR^j{}_lF^{kl}$; reading the dictionary and using $\det R=1$ in the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{nij}R^i{}_kR^j{}_lR^n{}_m=\epsilon_{klm}$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]) gives $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$. The general case is the actual unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii). Since components transform by multiplication with $\Lambda$, first apply $\widehat R$ and then $B(-\beta)$; the latter uses (a′) with vector velocity $-c\beta$, not the nonnegative axis parameter of (a). (d) Chain clauses (a)-(c) with [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: clause (a) of that theorem in both charts plus its clause (b) for the pair of descriptions. No potential, no second derivative of the fields, no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

consumer_reviews.statement: Let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and consider the constant fields of [[def-em-fields]] $$E:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3,\quad E\equiv E_0e_2,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ which form a source-free smooth solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (all first derivatives vanish and $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$). Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the boosted inertial chart of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]]. Then the components of the same field in $x'$ are $$E'=\gamma E_0\,e_2,\qquad B'=-\frac{\gamma\beta E_0}{c}\,e_3=-\frac{\gamma |v|E_0}{c^2}\,e_3,$$ so the moving observer reads an electric field of magnitude $\gamma E_0$ along $e_2$ and, for $\beta>0$, a nonzero magnetic field along $-e_3$: a purely electric uniform field acquires a magnetic component in the boosted description. The two invariants check directly: with the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2\Bigl(\frac{\beta^2E_0^2}{c^2}-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}\Bigr)=-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B,$$ using $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]). At $\beta=0$ the formulas reduce to $E'=E$, $B'=0$. The computation is exact for the constant field; the example reports no measurement, identifies no source producing the field, and asserts nothing about finite-energy or bounded configurations.
consumer_reviews.strategy: **Verification:** substitute the data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] with $\beta$ as given. Here $E_\parallel=0$, $B_\parallel=0$ since $E\perp e_1$ and $B=0$, and $v\times B=0$, while $v\times E=(\beta c e_1)\times(E_0e_2)=\beta cE_0e_3$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the boost formulas give $E'=\gamma E_0e_2$ and $B'=-\gamma |v|E_0e_3/c^2=-\gamma\beta E_0e_3/c$. The invariant values are computed with [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the identity $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]; the constant field is a solution of the source-free smooth branch because every displayed first derivative vanishes. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
