consumer_reviews.statement: Statement refuted: 'In the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the inertial chart x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3), the null plane H := {x^1 = x^0}, is a boundary of the model in the following three senses: (i) no future causal curve crosses from {x^1 > x^0} to {x^1 < x^0}; (ii) H separates all causal relations, so no event of {x^1 > x^0} is causally related to any event of {x^1 < x^0}; and (iii) the metric degenerates on H, so that H is a singular boundary of the spacetime on which the model fails.' Here H is the full causal-past boundary of the accelerated congruence; only its half-plane {x^1 = x^0 >= 0} belongs to the boundary of the right wedge W={x^1>|x^0|}. Counterexample: (a) A future timelike crossing refutes the causal separation claims. Let p := x^{-1}(-1,0,0,0) and q := x^{-1}(3,1,0,0), and let y: [0,1] -> A be the affine segment y(s) := p + s(q-p). The displacement q - p has chart components (4,1,0,0), so eta(q-p,q-p) = -16 + 1 = -15 < 0 and the time component is 4 > 0: the segment is a future timelike curve (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Its coordinate function x^0 - x^1 takes the values -1 at s = 0 and +2 at s = 1, hence vanishes at s = 1/3, at x^{-1}(1/3,1/3,0,0): a future timelike curve crosses H, refuting (i). Moreover q is in the causal future of p in the sense p <= q of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space, and p and q lie on opposite sides of H, so the segment relates events on opposite sides, refuting (ii). (b) Events of H and of its complement are causally related in both directions. The event r := x^{-1}(0,1,0,0) satisfies r < x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) because the displacement (1,0,0,0) is future timelike; and x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) < x^{-1}(2,3/2,0,0) because the displacement (1,1/2,0,0) satisfies -1 + 1/4 < 0 with positive time component (lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion (c)). The event x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) lies on H while r and x^{-1}(2,3/2,0,0) do not, so H neither separates causal relations nor consists of causally isolated events. (c) No metric degeneracy occurs. In the inertial chart the matrix of eta is the constant diag(-1,1,1,1) on the whole model, hence eta is nondegenerate and constant everywhere, in particular on H; and the actual crossing event x^{-1}(1/3,1/3,0,0) on the future timelike segment of (a) is an event of H on which the metric is the ordinary flat metric. It occurs at parameter 1/3, not at the midpoint of that segment. The Rindler map Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) with theta in R and rho > 0 is, by thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), a smooth bijection onto W with a smooth inverse; its domain simply satisfies rho > 0, so its coordinate domain omits rho = 0 and its image omits H; the wedge boundary consists only of the two null half-planes x^1 = |x^0| >= 0, whereas H is one of the full causal-horizon planes, and the failure of the map to be defined there is a property of the coordinate map, not of eta. (d) An inertial worldline crosses H. The worldline z(t) := x^{-1}(c t, 0, 0, 0) of the inertial frame satisfies z(0) = x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), which lies on H, and is defined and future timelike for every real t; thus a single regular worldline passes through H from the region x^1 > x^0 (for t < 0 it has x^1 = 0 > x^0 = c t) to the region x^1 < x^0 (for t > 0), which refutes (i) in a second way and contradicts the reading of H as a boundary on which the model fails. What remains true is exactly the conditional statement of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (ii), that the specific congruence worldlines cannot be reached from events with V >= 0; this is a restriction of causal reachability of those worldlines and not a boundary or singularity of the affine model. (e) Scope. All assertions are mathematical statements about the affine model and its causal reachability relations; no physical interpretation, measurement or empirical claim is made, and no choice principle is used.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Explicit witnesses checked against the coordinate criterion of lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion. (a) The affine segment y has constant derivative with coordinates (4,1,0,0); eta applied to it is -16+1=-15 < 0 and its time component is positive, so y is a future timelike curve by the definition of causal classification and the future cone; the coordinate function x^0 - x^1 along y is affine with values -1 and 2 at the endpoints, so it vanishes inside [0,1] and the crossing event y(1/3)=x^{-1}(1/3,1/3,0,0) lies on H. This is a direct refutation of the first two clauses of the quoted statement. (b) The displayed displacements (1,0,0,0) and (1,1/2,0,0) are future timelike, with norms -1 and -3/4 respectively by the coordinate criterion ((c) of the cited lemma), and the initial and final events straddle H while the middle event lies on it; r=(0,1,0,0) is explicitly off H. (c) Nondegeneracy and constancy of the metric matrix are read from the inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, def-sr-affine-minkowski-model); the domain property of Phi is clause (b) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples. The crossing event is at y(1/3), not the falsely identified midpoint. The inertial metric is nondegenerate at every event; restricting a coordinate chart to the wedge changes neither it nor the model domain. Distinguish the two half-plane portions of the wedge boundary from the full horizon planes, as in the repaired Rindler theorem. (d) The worldline z is affine with constant future timelike tangent (c,0,0,0), so it is a future timelike worldline defined for all t (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline), and the sign of x^0 - x^1 = c t changes at t = 0. (e) Scope only. No choice principle is used.
consumer_reviews.physical_scope: Counterexample within the flat classical model: the null coordinate boundary of the Rindler chart is shown to be a coordinate-map boundary rather than a boundary or singularity of the spacetime, and the only horizon statement concerning it is the causal restriction of reachability of particular congruence worldlines. No physical interpretation of the witnesses beyond the model's causal reachability is asserted, and no measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made.

consumer_reviews.statement: Statement refuted: 'For every pair of future timelike worldlines y and y' of the model for which the radar protocol of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol applies with y as observer and y' as reflector, the radar distance assigned by y to the reflection event on y' equals the radar distance assigned by y' to the reflection event on y; that is, the radar distance between two observers is symmetric under interchange of observer and reflector.' Counterexample in the Rindler chart of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar with y = O the worldline rho = rho_0 and y' = R the worldline rho = 2rho_0 (coaxial, with the same y = z = 0 coordinates), rho_0 > 0, c > 0. (a) Radar distance from O to R. Emit from O at the Rindler time theta_e = 0, i.e. from e_- = x^{-1}(0, rho_0, 0, 0). By pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) the reflection event on R is q_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) at Rindler time log 2 and the reception event on O is e_+ = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time 2 log 2; the round trip takes 2rho_0 log 2/c of O's proper time, so the radar distance assigned by O is D_1 := rho_0 log 2. (b) Radar distance from R to O. Emit from R at theta = 0, i.e. from r_- = x^{-1}(0, 2rho_0, 0, 0). The future null line from r_- towards O is the constant-U line with U = 2rho_0; it meets rho = rho_0 at the Rindler time log 2, at the reflection event q'_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/4, 5rho_0/4, 0, 0), and the return line reaches R at the Rindler time 2 log 2, at the event x^{-1}(15rho_0/4, 17rho_0/4, 0, 0). The round trip takes 4rho_0 log 2/c of R's proper time, so the radar distance assigned by R is D_2 := 2rho_0 log 2. (c) Hence D_2/D_1 = 2 = rho_m/rho_0: the two radar distances between the same pair of worldlines differ, and the assignment is not symmetric. Both assignments are finite and both reflection events lie in the causal future of their respective emission events; the asymmetry is a property of the radar assignment with the two different observers, not a physical anisotropy. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors; the symmetric half-split convention of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol is retained, and no measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Recompute the radar protocol of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the roles of the two worldlines interchanged. (a) Recompute directly from the theorem and chart: from (0,rho_0), the constant-V=-rho_0 ray meets rho=2rho_0 at theta=log2, giving q_m=(3rho_0/2,5rho_0/2); its constant-U return meets rho=rho_0 at theta=2log2, giving (15rho_0/8,17rho_0/8). Both displacements are future null. This uses no B-page example as a supplier. (b) The future null line from r_- towards smaller rho is the constant-U line U = 2rho_0, i.e. rho = 2rho_0 e^{-theta}; it meets rho = rho_0 at theta = log 2, and the chart coordinates there are (rho_0 sinh(log 2), rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/4, 5rho_0/4, 0, 0) by sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). The return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = 2rho_0 at theta = 2log 2, with coordinates (2rho_0 sinh(2log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/4, 17rho_0/4, 0, 0). The proper-time conversion factor on the worldline rho = const is rho/c per unit Rindler time by the proper-time formula in pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii), giving the round-trip proper times 2rho_0 log 2/c and 4rho_0 log 2/c respectively and the radar distances D_1 = rho_0 log 2 and D_2 = 2rho_0 log 2. (c) Since log2>log1=0, D1>0 and the quotient D_2/D_1=2 is well defined. The radius-dependent proper-time conversion factor, not any physical anisotropy, causes the two observer assignments to differ. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

consumer_reviews.statement: Worked computation in the Rindler chart of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar. Let c > 0, fix rho_0 > 0 and take y_0 = z_0 = 0; let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0 with Rindler time theta = c tau/rho_0, and take the emission event e_- at theta_e = 0, so that e_- = x^{-1}(0, rho_0, 0, 0) in the inertial chart x. (a) Reflector at rho_m = 2rho_0. The future null line from e_- of constant V has V = -rho_0, and it meets rho = 2rho_0 at the Rindler time theta_m = log 2; using sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives, thm-natural-logarithm-laws) the reflection event is q_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0), and the return event is e_+ = x^{-1}(rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time theta(e_+) = 2 log 2. Thus (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = log 2 = theta_m, the radar time assigned to q_m is (rho_0/c) log 2 plus the base constant of O's proper time, and the radar distance is rho_0 log 2. The two worldlines rho = rho_0 and rho = 2rho_0 are at rest distance rho_0 in the slice theta = log 2; since e > 2 gives log 2 < 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws), the radar distance is strictly smaller than the rest distance. (b) Reflector at rho_m = rho_0/2. The future null line from e_- of constant U has U = rho_0, and it meets rho = rho_0/2 at the Rindler time theta_m = log 2; using sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 the reflection event is q'_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0) and the return event is again e_+ = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time 2 log 2. The radar time is again (rho_0/c) log 2 plus the base constant and the radar distance is again rho_0 log 2, while the rest distance in the slice theta = log 2 is now rho_0/2; since e < 3 < 4 gives log 2 > 1/2 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws), the radar distance is now strictly larger than the rest distance. (c) The two cases (a)-(b) give the same radar distance $\rho_0\log2$ at distinct rest distances $\rho_0$ and $\rho_0/2$; this demonstrates noninjectivity of the assignment as the reflector radius varies. To prove that radar distance is not determined by the rest distance alone, also take $\rho_m=3\rho_0/2$. With the same emission at $\theta_e=0$, the reflection occurs at $\theta_m=\log(3/2)$, at $q''_m=x^{-1}(5\rho_0/8,13\rho_0/8,0,0)$, and the return occurs at $2\log(3/2)$, at $e''_+=x^{-1}(65\rho_0/72,97\rho_0/72,0,0)$. This reflector has rest distance $\rho_0/2$, equal to case (b), but radar distance $\rho_0\log(3/2)<\rho_0\log2$, because $3/2<2$ and log is strictly increasing. These equal inputs and unequal outputs prove the stated failure of dependence on rest distance alone. The original two cases both satisfy $\theta_m=(\theta_e+\theta(e_+))/2$ and have round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log2/c$; the third case satisfies the same midpoint identity and has round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log(3/2)/c$. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors in the flat classical model; no measurement, apparatus, source or statistical claim, and no empirical inference, is made, and the idealizations of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (v) are retained.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Substitute the two reflector radii into the exact radar computation of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii). (a) With theta_e = 0 the constant-V line through e_- carries V = -rho_0; meeting rho = 2rho_0 gives -2rho_0 e^{-theta} = -rho_0, i.e. e^{-theta} = 1/2 and theta_m = log 2; the chart coordinates of q_m are (2rho_0 sinh(log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) by the exact values sinh(log 2) = 3/4, cosh(log 2) = 5/4, which follow from the defining exponentials. The return line is the constant-U line through q_m and meets rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = 2log 2, giving e_+ = (rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) (sinh(2log 2) = 15/8, cosh(2log 2) = 17/8). The radar time and distance follow from the protocol formula of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the round-trip proper time rho_0(2log 2)/c of O; the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The inequality log 2 < 1 is the strict increase of log and 2 < e (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (b) With theta_e = 0 the constant-U line through e_- carries U = rho_0; meeting rho = rho_0/2 gives (rho_0/2) e^{theta} = rho_0, i.e. theta_m = log 2, and the reflection event is ((rho_0/2) sinh(log 2), (rho_0/2) cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0); the return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = rho_0 again at theta = 2log 2, giving the same return event as in (a). The radar quantities are as displayed, and log 2 > 1/2 follows from log4=2log2>log e=1, since 4 > e and log is strictly increasing (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (c) Cases (a)-(b) alone prove that distinct reflector radii and rest distances can give the same radar distance; they do not establish failure of dependence on rest distance alone. For the additional radius 3rho_0/2, constant V=-rho_0 gives theta_m=log(3/2). The defining exponentials give sinh(log(3/2))=5/12 and cosh(log(3/2))=13/12; multiplying by 3rho_0/2 gives (5rho_0/8,13rho_0/8). The return has theta=2log(3/2), for which e^theta=9/4 and e^(-theta)=4/9, hence sinh theta=65/72 and cosh theta=97/72; multiplying by rho_0 gives the stated return coordinates. The outgoing displacement from (0,rho_0) is (5rho_0/8,5rho_0/8), future null. The return displacement from q''_m is (5rho_0/18,-5rho_0/18), future null. The third reflector and the radius rho_0/2 reflector both have rest distance rho_0/2, while their radar distances are rho_0 log(3/2) and rho_0 log2, unequal by strict increase of log. This completes the full claim with all earlier examples and midpoint calculations preserved. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

consumer_reviews.statement: Consider the following hypothetical signalling model in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) with the SI coordinate conventions x^0 = c t (def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions). (S1) There are transmitters, each at rest in an inertial frame, that emit localized signals travelling at a fixed speed u with u > c in that frame, in any spatial direction. (S2) A received signal can be immediately re-emitted at the same event by a receiver, at speed u in the receiver's own rest frame (unrestricted receiving and relaying, no delay, no loss). (S3) Transmitters and receivers may move inertially at any speed v with 0 < v < c. (S4) The displacement between the emission and the reception event of a signal is a vector of the affine model, and displacements transform between inertial charts by the model's Lorentz transitions; the framework's kinematics is not modified. Then there is an explicit configuration in which a one-relay signal chain is received strictly before it was emitted: let L > 0, 0 < v < c and u > c satisfy v > 2u/(1 + u^2/c^2), which is possible because 2u/(1 + u^2/c^2) < c for u > c; let A rest at x^1 = 0 in an inertial chart x and let B move with the straight worldline x^1 = L + vt; emit a signal from A at the event A_0 = x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), in the direction of increasing x^1; let B receive it at the event B_1 and re-emit immediately toward A at speed u in B's rest frame. Then the following are exact identities of the model. (a) t(B_1) = L/(u - v) > 0 and x^1(B_1) = uL/(u - v) > 0, and the displacement B_1 - A_0 = (c t(B_1), x^1(B_1), 0, 0) is spacelike. (b) The return displacement in the chart x is (c Delta t, -x^1(B_1), 0, 0) with Delta t = x^1(B_1)(1 - vu/c^2)/(u - v), which is negative under the stated choice of v, and the arrival event A_1 on A's worldline satisfies t(A_1) = t(B_1) + Delta t = L(2u - v - v u^2/c^2)/(u - v)^2 < 0. (c) Hence A_1 - A_0 = (c t(A_1),0,0,0) with t(A_1) < 0, so A_1 lies in the strict chronological past I^-(A_0) of the emission event, and the return displacement B_1 - A_1 is spacelike. (d) In the model S1-S4 a signal chain therefore connects an emission event A_0 to an event A_1 in the strict past of A_0, and each leg's reception is spacelike-separated from its emission; by (c) of thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence the composition of the two legs is incompatible with the causal signal restriction post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, under which a reception event of a transmission lies in the causal future of its emission event and a relay chain cannot return to its own emission event (pthm-sr-causal-signal-order-and-composition(ii)-(iii)). So the hypothetical model S1-S4 and the causal signal restriction cannot both describe one and the same process family. (e) Scope and qualification. The computation is conditional on S1-S4 and is a kinematic identity about the hypothetical model; it is not a report of any observation, it does not establish that superluminal transmitters or receivers can be built or that tachyons exist, and it says nothing about processes that are not signals of the model: a prearranged pattern or configuration whose successive spacelike-separated events transfer no signal or energy between them (for example independently triggered devices, or a moving spot) is not covered, and no phase velocity, group velocity, shadow or geometric pattern is thereby claimed to be a signal. No quantum, gravitational, medium or detector effect is described, and no statistical or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.
consumer_reviews.strategy: Conditional deduction inside the hypothetical model; every step is an exact kinematic computation in one inertial chart and its boost-related chart. Set up the chart x of A's rest frame with x^0 = c t and x^1 in metres. (a) The receiver's worldline is the set x^1 = L + vt, which is future timelike because 0 < v < c (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion(c)); the outgoing signal at speed u in the direction of increasing x^1 is the ray x^1 = ut, so intersection gives t(B_1) = L/(u - v) > 0 and x^1(B_1) = uL/(u - v) > 0; the displacement B_1 - A_0 has eta((c t_1, u t_1, 0, 0)) = (u^2 - c^2) t_1^2 > 0, hence is spacelike by def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors. (b) In B's rest frame the return displacement is (c Delta t', -u Delta t') for the (positive) elapsed proper time Delta t' of the leg; transforming by the inverse passive boost (def-lorentz-boost and B(beta)^{-1} = B(-beta), lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, and the transformation law Delta x^0 = gamma(Delta x'^0 + beta Delta x'^1), Delta x^1 = gamma(Delta x'^1 + beta Delta x'^0) of the displayed matrix) gives c Delta t = gamma(c Delta t')(1 - vu/c^2) and x^1-displacement gamma Delta t'(v - u). The arrival lies on A's worldline x^1 = 0, so gamma Delta t'(v - u) = -x^1(B_1), i.e. Delta t' = x^1(B_1)/(gamma(u - v)) > 0; substituting gives Delta t = x^1(B_1)(1 - vu/c^2)/(u - v), which is negative exactly when v > c^2/u, and the threshold v > 2u/(1 + u^2/c^2) implies c^2/u < v because u > c (cross-multiplication). Adding t(B_1) = x^1(B_1)/u gives t(A_1) = L(2u - v - v u^2/c^2)/(u - v)^2, which is negative exactly under v > 2u/(1 + u^2/c^2); the direct substitution L(2u - v - vu^2/c^2)/(u - v)^2 with u > c and v satisfying the threshold is an exact rational-algebraic evaluation once u/c and v/c are treated as numbers. (c) A_1 - A_0 = (c t(A_1), 0, 0, 0) with t(A_1) < 0 is past timelike by the causal classification; the return displacement eta((c Delta t, -x^1(B_1), 0, 0)) = -c^2 Delta t^2 + x^1(B_1)^2 is positive because the leg is superluminal in B's rest frame and the transport preserves the causal character (thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra(iv), pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance). (d) The composition statement uses thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence(b)-(c) for the identification of reachability and the antisymmetry of <=, and pthm-sr-causal-signal-order-and-composition(ii)-(iii) for the physical reading of the restriction; the derivation shows A_1 in I^-(A_0) together with the two transmissions, which contradicts the restriction's requirement that each reception lie in the causal future of its emission, and contradicts (iii) applied to the composed chain. (e) records the exact conditional status, the non-signal configurations excluded from the conclusion, and the absence of any empirical or statistical content; no choice principle is used.

The computation is a conditional kinematic identity about that hypothetical model; it asserts nothing about realisable devices, observed tachyons, phase or group velocities, shadows, prearranged patterns without signal transfer, quantum or gravitational effects, and contains no measurement or statistical claim.
